segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎢᏃ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏓᏗᏬᏂᏏ, … Ꮭ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎤᏠᏯᏍᏛ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭᏭ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᎪᏍᏗ, ᏯᎾ,ᏕᏠᎦ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏕᏠ,Ꮖ ᎢᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎾᏍᏊ … ᎠᎾ,ᏝᏂᎬᏁ … ᎢᎩᏲᎱ,ᏎᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᏍᎪᎸᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ,’Ᏺ yeah… ᏳᏁᎩ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏩᎾ,ᏑᏴᏃ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ … [To Dianna] ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎪᏪᎵ, ᎠᏂᎧᎵᏏᏌ,?
segments.transliteration: hiino atsalagiha dadiwonisi, … tla yunega, utloyasdv atsalagihawu gesesdi, sgihena, gosdi, yana,detloga, ahani, tsidana,detlo,qua idiwonisgv tsalagi, nowule nasquu … ana,tlanigvne … igiyohu,sedi nigesvna, tsalagi, gawonihisdi, doyu, hena, squu asgolvgi yusdi,’yo yeah… yunegi nowule wana,suyvno aniwonihv nowule … [To Dianna] sgina, goweli, anikalisisa,?
segments.translation: We’re going to speak in Cherokee. Don’t include English, just all Cherokee. The reason being the ones that are going to school here, learning the language, they might learn something listening to us talk. Also, they are trying to keep us from losing the Cherokee language. It is really disappearing now. When they talk, they always include English. Also… [To Dianna] Did they fill out the papers?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The one where you only speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Okay. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᏍᏗᎧᎵᏏᏌ, ᎪᏪᎵ, … ᏍᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎨᏒᎢ … ᎯᎾ--ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏂᏅᏍᎪ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎩ, ᏳᏁᎩᎭ ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ … ᏙᎯ, ᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᏍᎬ … ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏥᏂᏓᏛᏁ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ--“ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩᏭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏁ
segments.transliteration: Okay. sgina desdikalisisa, goweli, … sdinohesgv, atsalagiha sdiwonisgi, gesvi … hina--igada, hena, doyu,’dv aninvsgo tla howa tsalagi, aniwonisgi, yigi, yunegiha yaniwonihi, sgina tla … dohi, nigvne,di una,dulisgv … doyu hena, anitsalagiha hena, ahani, tsinidadvne atsalagiha--“anitsalagiwu aniwonisgiwu iga” una,dvne
segments.translation: OK. You all filled out the papers, where you are saying that you are Cherokee speakers. We’ve seen some that don’t really speak Cherokee fluently. All they speak is English. That’s what they’re trying to stop from happening. Really, what we are doing is just the Cherokee speakers. “We want only the Cherokee speakers,” they said.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Do they have a school here in Tahlequah?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᎢᏭ ᏗᏢ, ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ,
segments.transliteration: ahani ditlv, na diniyotli, gehv dohv? aiwu ditlv, tsuna,tana,
segments.translation: Over on this [gestures] side is where the kids are, ain’t it? And on this [gestures] side are the adults.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎥ yeah ᎠᎬᏱ ᏓᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᏂ, ‘Ꮩ ᏕᏍᏓᏙ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎬᏗ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩᏃ? ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏕᏍᏓ--?
segments.transliteration: vv yeah agvyi dasdvyadvdvni, ‘do desdado yunega, gvdi, atsalagino? ‘do usdi desda--?
segments.translation: Uh-huh, yeah. The first thing I’m going to ask you all: What are y’alls names? In English and then in Cherokee, what are they?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Liw(i).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Liw(i). And in English?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: In English.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Oh, Leroy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Leroy...?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Sanders.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But Liwi is your Cherokee name. OK, yeah. That’s right. And what about you?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Tsetlug(i).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Tsetlug(i).

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Felix Sanders.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Felix Sanders. You always yelling?
[laughter]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-huh. All the time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who named you Tsetlug(i)?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎡᏥ’Ꮫ ᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎨᎵ ᏓᏬᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: etsi’dv geli tsigehv etsi tsigehv geli dawov sgina
segments.translation: I think it was my mom. I think she named me that. She said I was always yelling when I was little.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You were always yelling.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: They said I was always yelling. When I was little.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You were a crybaby. [laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎭᏢ … ᏍᏓᏕᏁ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎯᎳ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: hatlv … sdadene nowule hila tsudetiyvsadisv gehe?
segments.translation: Where were you all born? And what year was it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ’Ᏺ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ ᏓᎵᏆ ᏣᏩᏕᏅ the--ᎤᏪᏘ, hospital
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv’yo agvyi aha,ni daliqua tsawadenv the--uweti, hospital
segments.translation: Well, me first, I was born here in Tahlequah at the Old Hospital.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The hospital that was there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: ’56. And what about you?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎮᏍᏗ, … Ꮎ hospital ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᏱᎩ, ᎾᏅ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv hesdi, … na hospital awadenv yigi, nanv
segments.translation: Me, I wasn’t born in a hospital.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: At your house?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: No, at my grandma’s house.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: In Bunch.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Flute Springs *ᎠᎭᏂ,* -- *ᎠᎭᏂᏅ,* Bunch-Ꭲ Ꮭ ᎪᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ--
segments.transliteration: Flute Springs *ahani,* -- *ahaninv,* Bunch-i tla gosdi, nowule--
segments.translation: Here [gestures] is Flute Springs and here [gestures] is Bunch. There was nothing there...

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Just trees...

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: ...except woods.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You were born in the woods?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah. September 1, 1947.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: ‘47. We are about the same age, right?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: You were born in ‘46, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Boy, that’s an old number.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where did you all grow up?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎠᎬᏱ … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ Fog Hollow ᏣᏃᏎᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv agvyi … tla yawanv,ta, yitsanv,ta, na Fog Hollow tsanosehv
segments.translation: Me, I don’t know if you know it, but it’s Fog Hollow.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Fog Hollow?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ when I-- ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ” ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᏩᏙᏓ,(4:05) ᎯᏲᎵᎩᏍ ᎨᎲ? ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ,
segments.transliteration: una tsotsinelv when I-- agi,sdi tsigehv “godawasga” hena, dudov awadoda, hiyoligis gehv? sgina godawasga,
segments.translation: That’s where we lived when I was little. Godawasg(a) was my dad’s name. Did you know him, Godawasg(a)?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I think so.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: His mom was my sister.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, OK!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: He is my uncle.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, ᏣᏗᏍᎬ ‘Ꮩ ᏚᏙᎡ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎬᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: sgina godawasga, tsadisgv ‘do dudoe yonega, gvdi,?
segments.translation: That Godawasg(a) you’re talking about, what was his English name?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Johnny.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꭳ yeah! Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏥᏲᎵᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: o yeah! na’dv tsiyoligv osda, tsigehv sgina
segments.translation: Oh, yeah! I knew him well!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏴ, ᎥᎩᏙ ᎨᎲ -- ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎯᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: usdayvhvsgi, hena, sgina, ayv, vgido gehv -- uwetsi, hinana
segments.translation: His wife was my sister; this is her son.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Her name was Kal(i)sday(a), my mom.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I knew both of them.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Oh, really?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And that Charlie Shell?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: That would be my…uncle?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [To Guy] Yeah, that’s his uncle, Charlie.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Stanely, Joyce, and all of them.
segments.transliteration: Stanely, Joyce, and all of them.
segments.translation: Stanely, Joyce, and all of them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, Ꮎ David ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏥᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ ᎾᎥ ᎮᎾ, ᎪᏍᏗ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎠᏴ, ᎡᏥ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Pettit ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ, ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nahena, na David ahani, tsidulvwi,sdane nav hena, gosdi, tsosdadadvne,di ayv, etsi hena, tsigehv Pettit hena, ayv, etsi tsigehv
segments.translation: That David, the one that works here, he’s my close kinfolk. My late mother was a Pettit.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh! I didn’t know that.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, Ꮎ Pigeon Pettit that’s his grandpa ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Pigeon Pettit’Ꭾ ᎠᏴ, was my uncle.
segments.transliteration: nahena, na Pigeon Pettit that’s his grandpa gehv sgina Pigeon Pettit’he ayv, was my uncle.
segments.translation: That Pigeon Pettit, David’s grandpa, he was my uncle.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh! You all are real close kin.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Pettit—Pettit ᎡᏥ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Pettit ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Pettit—Pettit etsi hena, tsigehv Pettit gehv
segments.translation: My mother was a Pettit.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ Pettit ᎨᎲ … … ᏃᏭ ᎮᎾ, … ᏣᏗᎲ ᎩᎳ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾᎡ ᏗᏍᏓᏛᏏᏙᎸ … ᎦᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗᏓᏁ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏥᏕᏍᏓᏛᏏᏗᏒ? … ᎾᎥᏭ’Ꭸ ᏓᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᎮ ‘ᏙᎨ?
segments.transliteration: o Pettit gehv … … nowu hena, … tsadihv gila iyusdi, unae disdadvsidolv … gadohv usdidane nahiyu tsigesv tsidesdadvsidisv? … navwu’ge dadanelv anehe ‘doge?
segments.translation: Oh, she was a Pettit. You all just said where you all grew up at. What was it like there, when you were growing up? Were there other houses nearby, or what?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Us, where we lived, it was the only house there. A little bitty house. Lights

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was the only house there?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᏍᏗᎢ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏗᏨᏍᏗ, ᎮᏍᏗ,--
segments.transliteration: Yeah, usdii hena, gali,tsode tsigehv … ditsvsdi, hesdi,--
segments.translation: Yeah, a little bitty house. Lights...

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all didn’t have lights?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, or water.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all didn’t have water in the house?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah. And the bathroom was outside.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The bathroom was set outside.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah. ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ Daddy ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, ᎦᏚᎲ ᏥᏫ,ᎦᎶᏍᎬ trying to find work.
segments.transliteration: Yeah. sgi yusdi awadvsv Daddy godawasga, gaduhv tsiwi,galosgv trying to find work.
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how it was when I grew up. Daddy, Godawasg(a), he would go to town to look for work.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, he was looking for work.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ … ᏒᎯᏰ ᏃᏭ ᏴᎦᎷᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎥᎾ--ᎥᎾ ᏃᏭ ᏦᎦᏓᏅᏒ Stilwell ᏃᏭ ᏥᏬᎩᎶᏒ … Stilwell ᏃᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ ᏃᏭ … ᎠᏴ, Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, job ᏄᏮᏅ but, we went to Chicago. Chicago ᏥᏬᏥᏁᎸ ᏞᎦ, and ᎡᏚᏗ … ᏌᏭ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏙᏆᎴᎷ ᏣᏆ,ᎩᎸᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ “hobo” Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, hobos ᏣᏁᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎮᎾ, … ᏍᎩ ᏣᎩᏍᎬ Ꮎ ticket – They wouldn’t let me, Ꮎ cause I was too young.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, tsulvwi,sdane,di … svhiye nowu yvgaluga, tsigehv … vna--vna nowu tsogadanvsv Stilwell nowu tsiwogilosv … Stilwell nowu gehv tsotsinelv nowu … ayv, tla doyu, yawanv,ta, job nuwvnv but, we went to Chicago. Chicago tsiwotsinelv tlega, and edudi … sawu hena, yuwaga,da, doqualelu tsaqua,gilvnv nahiyu “hobo” tsi,quisdi, hobos tsanehv nahiyu agvyi adela, hena, … sgi tsagisgv na ticket – They wouldn’t let me, na cause I was too young.
segments.translation: Yeah, work. He would come home late in the evening. When we moved, we moved to Stilwell. When we were living in Stilwell I don’t know what kind of job he got. But, we went to Chicago, We lived in Chicago for a little while. My grandpa... One time, I got on a train and met a hobo. That’s when a lot of them were around. At first, he was getting money to buy a ticket. They wouldn’t let me [ride] because I was too young.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, underage.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: And then, ᏔᎵᏁ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ hobo ᏥᏥᏩᏛᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ--
segments.transliteration: And then, taline tsinawadvnelv hobo tsitsiwadvhv sgina--
segments.translation: And then, when I did it the second time, I found a hobo...

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: To help you?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, one-way ticket to Stilwell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You got off in Stilwell?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎾᏅ, hobo ᏧᏣᎥ ᏥᏭᎾᏂᎩᏒ and ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏒ’Ꮕ, ᎡᏚᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᎯᎾ, ᎤᏙᏓ, [ᏤᏡᎩ] ᎢᎾ ᏥᏩᎩᎶᏒ
segments.transliteration: awvsa, nanv, hobo tsutsav tsiwunanigisv and tsuna,delahosv’nv, edudi, hena, tsiganelv hina, udoda, [tsetlugi] ina tsiwagilosv
segments.translation: Just me, I guess, and that hobo stayed on the train. When they found out my grandpa lived there. His dad [Felix]. That’s where I went.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How long did you ride on the train?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Hmm…about two days.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: TWO DAYS! ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏣᏣᏩᏗᏎ hobo ᏍᏓᎵᎪᎮ
segments.transliteration: TWO DAYS! sgi yigohida, tsatsawadise hobo sdaligohe
segments.translation: TWO DAYS! That’s how long you rode with that hobo?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, I was with the hobo.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You were pretending to be a hobo, too?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ,--ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮫ (….?)[8:10] ᎯᎢ” [ᎤᏛᏅ] … ᎢᎾ--ᎢᎾ’Ꮓ ᏣᏩᏠᏒ Ꮎ Stilwell ᎡᏚᏗ, ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᏣᎩ,ᏐᎮᎸ’Ꮕ … Daddy--ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, ᎧᎵ,ᏍᏓᏯ,--Mom and Dad, they come and got me. ᏨᎩᎸᏂᎸᎢ
segments.transliteration: edoda,--edoda, hena, tsitsiyohehv “uneli,dv (….?) hii” [udvnv] … ina--ina’no tsawatlosv na Stilwell edudi, tsiganelv una tsiwagilutsv tsagi,sohelv’nv … Daddy--godawasga, kali,sdaya,--Mom and Dad, they come and got me. tsvgilvnilvi
segments.translation: When I told my dad, “Gross [unclear],” [he said.] I got off at Stilwell, where my grandpa lived. That’s where I went. He got on to me. And Daddy...Godawasg(a) and Kal(i)sday(a), my parents came and got me. They whupped me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: ‘Cause you ran away?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: About a month—Month later, ᎤᏠᏱ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ and ᎡᏚᏗ ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ -- I didn’t like it, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮥ ᎤᎾ Chicago. And they just—my grandpa ᎦᏏᏁᎦ, ᏥᏚᏙᎥ
segments.transliteration: About a month—Month later, utloyi tsinawadvnelv and edudi tsiwagilutsv -- I didn’t like it, hesdi, yagilvquo,de una Chicago. And they just—my grandpa gasinega, tsidudov
segments.translation: About a month later, I did the same thing. I got to my grandpa’s house. I didn’t like it in Chicago. And they just...my grandpa, his name was Gasineg(a).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gasineg(a), yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗᏅ and I stayed there until he died.
segments.transliteration: sgina, tsagi,sdelvhv tsuna,delo,quasdinv and I stayed there until he died.
segments.translation: He helped me go to school. I stayed there until he died.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Automobile-ᎢᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏨᏂᎸ ᎢᎾ ᏙᎲ? Chicago.
segments.transliteration: Automobile-idv squu tsvnilv ina dohv? Chicago.
segments.translation: Automobile hit you in Chicago, didn’t it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah. Chicago car ᏍᏊ ᏣᏮᏂᎸ (….) wheelchair-Ꭲ ᏣᏩᏣᏅ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. Chicago car squu tsawvnilv (….) wheelchair-i tsawatsanv
segments.translation: Yeah. A car hit me in Chicago. [unclear] . I was in a wheelchair.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Uh-huh, yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: It’s nasty there, Chicago.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏓᎾ,ᏙᏛᏙ yeah. Ꮭ ᎢᎦ ᏲᏚᎵ ᎢᎾ ᎠᏕᏗ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ’Ᏺ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, dana,dodvdo yeah. tla iga yoduli ina adedi ana,diho’yo
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what they say. You wouldn’t want to live there, they say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏱᏮᎧᏅᏬᎦ,’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎳ, ᏱᎩ, ᏙᎲ? ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᏪᏙᎸ ᎠᏴ
segments.transliteration: yiwvkanvwoga,’dv squu gola, yigi, dohv? sawu yuwaga,da, awedolv ayv
segments.translation: You freeze there when it’s winter, ain’t it? I went there once.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: We lived there a long time, didn’t we?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: You ran away and rode with a hobo. [laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He was with a hobo.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: There were a lot of them, then, hobos.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ … ᎾᏃᎲ--ᎠᎪᎾ’Ꭸ ᏗᏍᏗᎶᏎ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu,dv … nanohv--agona’ge disdilose sgi yigohidi,?
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. What about... were you all once starving coming in the train?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were there train stops?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎩᏢ Ꮎ hobo ᏍᏊ ᏥᏥᏰᎶᎲ ᎣᏍᏛ’Ᏺ ᏦᎩᎾ,ᎵᏲᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮧ, ᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ ᏥᎨᎲ but ᏍᏗᎵᏪᎵ’Ꭱ ᏣᎩ,ᏘᏃᏢ … ᏣᏩᏠᏒ’Ꮕ, ᏧᏣᎥᏭ ᏥᏩᎥ(10:34)
segments.transliteration: Yeah, adela, hena, tsagitlv na hobo squu tsitsiyelohv osdv’yo tsogina,liyohv asenv, uneli,di, hena,’yo tsigehv but sdiliweli’e tsagi,tinotlv … tsawatlosv’nv, tsutsavwu tsiwav
segments.translation: I had money. I was feeding the hobo, too. We were good friends, but he was nasty. But he brought me all the way to Stilwell. When I got off, he just stayed on the train.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He went down south?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He had it made, you feeding him.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, he was eating well.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And you never saw him again?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏔᎵᏁ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᏄᏓᎴ -- ᏄᏓᎴ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎧᎵ,ᏍᏓᏯ, my mom -ᎡᏥ. Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏚᏓ, who raised me.
segments.transliteration: taline tsinawadvnelv nudale -- nudale tsigehv … asenv, kali,sdaya, my mom -etsi. na squu agiduda, who raised me.
segments.translation: When I did it again, it was different. But Kal(i)sday(a), my mom. And my grandpa, who raised me.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Which one whupped you? Did Kal(i)sday(a) whup you, or was it Godawasg(a)?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎡᏧᎳ, ᏥᎬᎩ,ᏖᏆᎶᏅ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … I think, let’s see, ᏌᏚ’Ꮫ ᎾᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: etsula, tsigvgi,tequalonv (uniyetsi,sgv) … I think, let’s see, sadu’dv nawadetiyvda, tsigehv
segments.translation: They both attacked me. [laughter] … I think, let’s see, I think I was 11 years old then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎦᏳᎳ, ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎭᏨᏏᏰᏍᎨ? Well I’ll be!
segments.transliteration: gayula, sgi iga hatsvsiyesge? Well I’ll be!
segments.translation: You were already roaming around like that? Well, I’ll be!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ,’Ꮫ truck Ꮎ ᏧᏔᎾ, trucks ᏥᏓᎩ,ᏟᏙᎸ retired ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ 25 years ᏣᎩᎯᎵᏙᎸ
segments.transliteration: gayu,la,’dv truck na tsutana, trucks tsidagi,tlidolv retired tsinawadvnelv 25 years tsagihilidolv
segments.translation: I’m already retired. I drove big trucks for 25 years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: 25 years! Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏤᏙᎵᏙᎸ Ꮎ truck
segments.transliteration: 25 years! Yeah, doyu’dv tsedolidolv na truck
segments.translation: 25 years! You been all over the place.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Coast to coast, to Canada, just everywhere.
segments.transliteration: Coast to coast, to Canada, just everywhere.
segments.translation: Coast to coast, to Canada, just everywhere.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏁᎳᏚ’Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏂᎯ ᏌᏚ … ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏂᏕᎩᎾ,ᏓᎸ ᏙᎲ? ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, -- ᏌᏚ ᏱᏣᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏚ ᏁᎳᏚ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ‘Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎨᏙᎮ Ᏹ-Ᏹ-ᏱᏫᎬᏯᎾ,ᏖᏎ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv neladu’tlv yawadetiyvda, nihi sadu … tsanela, tsudetiyvda, nidegina,dalv dohv? tsanela, tsudetiyvda, -- sadu yitsadetiyvda, gali,quadu neladu’le yigi, ‘tlv yawadetiyvda, gehv ayv, … ayv, hena, yigedohe yi-yi-yiwigvyana,tese
segments.translation: I was around 18 years old and you were 11. We are about eight years apart. Eight years. When you were 11, I was about 17 or 18. If I was there, I would’ve kicked you.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎦᎾ,ᏰᎩ, ᏂᏣᏛᏅᏕᎨ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏣᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: doyu squu gana,yegi, nitsadvnvdege sgi iga yitsadetiyvda, dohv?
segments.translation: You were in a dangerous situation, for being that age, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Well back then…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: …people weren’t that mean.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, ᏯᎾ,ᏓᎷᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎾᏅ truck ᏣᎩᎯᎵᏙᎸ ᎾᏅ Walmart ᏣᎩᎯᎵᏙᎸ Ꮎ-Ꮎ Sam Walton ᏍᎩ he’s the one that gave me the job.
segments.transliteration: gohiyv tsigi, yana,daluga, hena, gohi tsigi, nanv truck tsagihilidolv nanv Walmart tsagihilidolv na-na Sam Walton sgi he’s the one that gave me the job.
segments.translation: Nowadays, people kill each other. I drove trucks for Walmart. That Sam Walton, he’s the one that gave me the job.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Stilwell ᏥᏥᏯᎥ restaurant-Ꭲ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, car ᏣᎯᎵᏙᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, “ᏫᎷᏨᎢ” ᏣᏬᏎᎸ Ꮎ restaurant-Ꭲ ᎢᎾ ᏧᏬᏢ’Ꮕ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᎾᎥ ᏧᏬᏢ he looked—looked like a homeless to me.
segments.transliteration: Stilwell tsitsiyav restaurant-i na utanida, tsosdadanvtli, car tsahilidohv sgina, “wilutsvi” tsawoselv na restaurant-i ina tsuwotlv’nv tsosdadanvtli, utanida, udvhisdi nav tsuwotlv he looked—looked like a homeless to me.
segments.translation: I was in a restaurant in Stilwell. My older brother was driving a car. “Go to the restaurant,” he told me. He was sitting there at the restaurant, my older brother, with an old man. He looked like a homeless man, to me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, Sam Walton.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: “My name is Sam Walton,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “Yeah, ᎭᎵ,ᏍᎪᏍᎦ,’Ꮫ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏎᏅ, driver’s license ᏧᎴᏒ
segments.transliteration: “My name is Sam Walton,” tsawohelv “Yeah, hali,sgosga,’dv” tsiyohelv asenv, driver’s license tsulesv
segments.translation: “My name is Sam Walton,” he told me. “Yeah, you are lying,” I told him. He took his driver’s license out.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏌᏭ ᏥᏲᎵᎦ, … “ᏯᏴᏟᎦ,’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏗ,’Ꮲ ᎤᏪᏘ, pickup ᎤᏦᏙ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᎩᏟ ᏃᏭᎴ--
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv sgi nusdv ana,diho na’e sawu tsiyoliga, … “yayvtliga,’dv tsigehv tsunali,sdayvdi,’tlv uweti, pickup utsodo” adihv gitli nowule--
segments.translation: That’s how he was, they say. I knew someone … he said, “He [Sam Walton] would come into a restaurant. He drove an old pickup.” And a dog...

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, he had an old pickup.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: “ᎩᏟ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᏣ pickup-Ꭲ” ᏣᏗᏍᎬ “ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ, ᏂᎯ, ᏥᏂᎬᏩ,ᏍᏗ, ᏂᎬᏩ,ᏍᏙ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏓᏌᎳᏗ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎡᎳᏗᏴ ᎡᏙᎲ ᎨᎲ” ᏣᏬᏎᎰ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: “gitli nowule dutsa pickup-i” tsadisgv “etsulaha hena, ayv, nihi, tsinigvwa,sdi, nigvwa,sdo dikana,di” tsadihv “asenv, doyu, hena, tla doyu, udasaladi, yigehe nahena, eladiyv edohv gehv” tsawoseho’dv
segments.translation: “And there’d be a dog riding with him,” he said. “He was just like us. He wasn’t uppity, he was normal like us,” he used to tell me.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏥᏩᎩ,ᏘᏂᏙᎸ Ꮎ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᎤᏔᎾ,’Ꭱ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎠᏩᎪᏛᏗ ᎨᎵᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, it was just a regular home.
segments.transliteration: una tsuwenvsv tsiwagi,tinidolv na gali,tsode tsuwenvhv utana,’e gali,tsode awagodvdi gelihv asenv, it was just a regular home.
segments.translation: He took me to his house. I thought he was going to show me a big house, but it was just a regular home.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, security Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏣᏁᏙᎲ … ᏗᏂ,ᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ, ᎤᎾᎦ,ᏎᏍᏗᏕᎬ
segments.transliteration: asenv, security tsi,quisdi, tsanedohv … dini,daniyisgi, unaga,sesdidegv
segments.translation: But there were a lot of security there. Security was watching his home.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They were looking out.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: In 19-…1999 retired ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ I was young. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ’Ꮕ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏉᏢᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ’Ꮕ how to make it work.
segments.transliteration: In 19-…1999 retired tsinawadvnelv I was young. sgina, tsagi,sdelvhv’nv adela, hena, tsi,quisdi, aquotlvnv sgina, tsagi,sdelvhv’nv how to make it work.
segments.translation: I retired in 1999. I was young. He helped me a lot. I made a lot of money, and he helped me make it work.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The old man had money…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Now, I’ve got 600 acres.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: That’s what I got now. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ’Ꮕ Ꮎ ᎠᏕᎳ,
segments.transliteration: That’s what I got now. sgina, tsagi,sdelvhv’nv na adela,
segments.translation: That’s what I got now. He helped me with the money.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: 25 years.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I drove 25 years.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Walmart truck.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘ᏙᎲ ᎠᏁᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ, ᏣᏗᎲ ᏂᎬ ᏤᏙᎵᏙᎸ ᎯᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮓ ᏣᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬ ᎯᏣᎳᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᎨᏣ,ᏛᏛᎮᏢᏍᎨ’Ꭸ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: ‘dohv anelisgv aniyvwi, tsadihv nigv tsedolidolv hitsalagi’no tsana,delahosgv hitsalagi, gehv getsa,dvdvhetlvsge’ge gohu,sdi,?
segments.translation: What you’re saying, you driving all over, what did people think when they found out you were Cherokee? Did they ask you a bunch of questions?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎾᏅ Hayes, Kansas Ꮵ-ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ … ᏧᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎤᎾ Ꮳ-ᏣᏬᏢ ᎾᏅ ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏣᏂᎶᏍᎬᏭ … ᏌᏭ ᏥᏥᎴᏫᏍᏙᏔᏅ “ᎠᎩᏲᏏ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏎᏅ, they wouldn’t…
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nanv Hayes, Kansas tsi-tsiwagilutsv … tsunali,sdayv,di una tsa-tsawotlv nanv tsunilvwi,sdanehv tsanilosgvwu … sawu tsitsilewisdotanv “agiyosi squu ayv,” tsitsiyohelv asenv, they wouldn’t…
segments.translation: When I got to Hayes, Kansas, at a restaurant, I was sitting there and the workers were going by. I stopped one of them. “I’m hungry, too,” I told them. But they weren’t…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They weren’t paying attention to you.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: They were racists. Cause I was--ᏥᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏥᏓᏩᏟᏴᎲ’Ꮓ the manager ᏧᎷᏨ’Ꮓ ᎤᎾ-ᎤᎾ ᏣᏬᏢ ᎤᎾ Ꮎ ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏥᎦᏙᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏣᏥᏌᏗᏅᏕ
segments.transliteration: They were racists. Cause I was--tsitsalagi, tsigehv asenv, tsidawatliyvhv’no the manager tsulutsv’no una-una tsawotlv una na tsulvwi,sdanehv tsigadogv una tsatsisadinvde
segments.translation: They were racists. I was Cherokee. But I spoke my mind to the manager. He came. I was sitting there and the waiter was standing nearby. And he fired him right then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? Well, I’ll be!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: “ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏱᏥᏍᏚᎲᎦ, ᎠᎭᏂ, restaurant” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ the manager. “ᏥᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ, but I’ve got a brain, too!” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: “gila yigohida, yitsisduhvga, ahani, restaurant” tsitsiyohelv the manager. “tsitsalagi, hena, ayv, but I’ve got a brain, too!” tsitsiyohelv
segments.translation: “I can shut down this restaurant real quick,” I told the manager. “I am Cherokee, but I’ve got a brain, too!”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: You mean you hadn’t lost it? [laughs]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: But I got to eat for free.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They fed you for free!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ North Carolina ᏥᏬᎩᎶᏒ North Carolina ᎾᏅ’Ꮫ North Carolina ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, they…
segments.transliteration: una’dv squu North Carolina tsiwogilosv North Carolina nanv’dv North Carolina anitsalagi, they…
segments.translation: Also, North Carolina, we went to North Carolina. Those North Carolina Cherokees…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: …they speak….

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: …they speak different.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: They’ve got an accent.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You can hardly understand it.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎪᎳ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ … Ꮶ-ᏦᎩᎾ,ᎵᎪᏅ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ “I don’t know. This is the way you supposed to talk,” ᏣᏬᏎᎲ “You’re not talking it. ᏄᏓᎴ ᎯᏬᏂᎯ,” ᏣᏬᏎᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏁᎵᎲ’Ꮓ ᏥᏯ,ᏓᏱᏅᏒ
segments.transliteration: gola’e tsigehv sawu … tso-tsogina,ligonv ageya, atsalagi, tsigehv asenv, nudale aniwonihv “I don’t know. This is the way you supposed to talk,” tsawosehv “You’re not talking it. nudale hiwonihi,” tsawosehv sgina, tsinelihv’no tsiya,dayinvsv
segments.translation: Last winter, I was with one woman, a Cherokee. But they talk different. “I don’t know. This is the way you supposed to talk,” she told me. “You don’t talk it. You talk different,” she said. That made me mad at her, so I got rid of her.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I made her get out next to the highway. [laughs]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ [To Dianna] ᏤᏙᎸ’Ꮂ Ꮭ’ᎨᏲ?
segments.transliteration: doyu,’dv squu naniwesgo nudale nusdi, uniwonihisdi, ana,diho [To Dianna] tsedolv’hv tla’geyo?
segments.translation: That’s what they say, they speak different, their language. [To Dianna] You’ve been there before, right?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Yeah. Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏱᎪᎵᎨ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎢᎦᏓ,’Ꭱ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎣᏏ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ, ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ-
segments.transliteration: Yeah. tla howa yigolige naniwesgv igada,’e osda, osi aniwonihv, asenv, tla-
segments.translation: Yeah. I didn’t really understand what they were saying. Some of them speak alright but…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ I guess … ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏱᎨᏙᎲ, ᎤᎾ… Maybe.
segments.transliteration: ayv,’dv I guess … nigohilv yigedohv, una… Maybe.
segments.translation: Me, I guess, if I’m there all the time… Maybe.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: …yeah, ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮺ ᏱᏬᏂᎯ, ᎡᎵᏭ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎾᏅᏁ
segments.transliteration: …yeah, utloyi’we yiwonihi, eliwu, asenv, doyu,’dv nudale nanvne
segments.translation: …you’d be speaking the same way. But they really do speak different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And how about you? Where did you grow up?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎯᎾ Bunch-Ꭲ ᎤᎾᎾ … ᏂᎬ’Ꮫ ᏦᏣᏓᏅᏏᏙᎲ and then ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏗᏗᏍᎩ, Ꮎ railroad track Ꮵ-ᏥᎪᏢᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: utloyi’dv yusdi, etsulaha yusdi, sgina vgido uwetsi, hina Bunch-i unana … nigv’dv tsotsadanvsidohv and then edoda tsigehv na didisgi, na railroad track tsi-tsigotlvgv, tsigehv
segments.translation: The same as him, because this is my sister’s boy. Bunch and then we just moved here and there all the time. My late father, he made railroad ties.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ yeah, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: o yeah, doyu,’dv sgi tsinana,dvnehv tsigehv etiyv adela, anotlvsgv
segments.translation: Oh, yeah, that’s what they used to do back then to make money.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Beans and potatoes and homemade biscuits is how we grew up.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah-lee!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏑᏍᏗ’Ꮕ, ᎡᏥ ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ y’know ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎣᎦᏛᏒ … y’know … ᎪᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎩ, Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, Ꮎ ᏚᏯ ᏚᏂᏫᏒ ᎠᏂ,’Ꮕ, y’know ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ--
segments.transliteration: asusdi’nv, etsi tsigotlvsgv tsigehv y’know sgi yusdi, ogadvsv … y’know … gogi, hena, yigi, na aniyonega, na duya duniwisv ani,’nv, y’know una’dv--
segments.translation: And my mom would make gravy. That’s how we grew up. In the summer, there were white people and they had beans and strawberries…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: …you picked them? You were finding money.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎩᏄᏗ,Ꮨ,’Ꮫ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏓᎩᏢ’Ꮕ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: ginudi,ti,’dv tsi,quisdosv gehv adela, dagitlv’nv squu
segments.translation: We had a lot quarters from them paying us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah … all day.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ … ᎠᏰᏟ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ -- 50 cents an hour, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ grocery ᎠᏓᎾᏅ ᏥᏬᎩᎶᏒ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ … ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏳᏓᎨᏛ, ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, … ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏳᏓᎨᏛ, ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ This was late ’49, ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏃᏥᎥ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ ᏦᎢ ᏨᎩᏙ ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏃᏥᎥ ᎠᏴ … ᎤᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎣᏂᏭ ᎨᎯ, ᏃᏭ, ᏂᎦᏓ, … Ꮟ … ᎤᏔᏂᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎦᏃᏍᎩᏍᎩ, ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎦᏃᏍᎩᏍᎩ, ᏙᏳ’ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏚᏙᎡ ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, (…) ᎦᏃᏍᎩᏍᎩ, … ᏔᎵᏁᎢ ᎡᎯ, ᏤᎩ, and ᏦᎢᏁᎢ’Ꮕ, - ᏦᎢᏁᎢ’Ꮕ, ᎧᎵ,ᏍᏓᏯ, Ꮎ ᎤᏥ [Leroy] ᎯᎢᎾ … ᎠᎵ’Ꮕ, … Sue-ᎢᏅ, ᏦᎢ,-ᏦᎢ, ᏨᎩᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ y’know…
segments.transliteration: vv … ayetli’dv tsigehv -- 50 cents an hour, nahiyu tsigehv … ganvdadiho na grocery adananv tsiwogilosv ganvdadiho sginana … hisgi, yudagedv, kali,setsi, … hisgi, yudagedv, kali,setsi, sgohi, iyadanv,di, tsigehv This was late ’49, edoda, nigohilv’dv yusdi, dulvwi,sdanehv hisgi, notsiv hisgi, otsatlanvtla tsoi tsvgido tsanela, notsiv ayv … usdi gehv ayv, sgina nigada, oniwu gehi, nowu, nigada, … si … utanida,’dv ganosgisgi, tsidudov ganosgisgi, doyu’hena, osda, dudoe gila yigohida, (…) ganosgisgi, … talinei ehi, tsegi, and tsoinei’nv, - tsoinei’nv, kali,sdaya, na utsi [Leory] hiina … ali’nv, … Sue-inv, tsoi,-tsoi, tsvgido gehv hisgi, otsatlanvtla y’know…
segments.translation: Yeah, we worked all day and got paid 50 cents an hour, back then. I remember when we went to the grocery store, a 5lb bag of sugar was 10 cents. This was late ’49. My late father, he was always working. There are five of us brothers. And three sisters. There were eight of us. I was the baby. I’m the last-born. The oldest, his name was Ganosgisg(i). He had a good name. […] [laughs] Ganosgisg(i) … then the second one was Tseg(i), the third one was Kal(i)sday(i) that was his [Leroy] mom. Then there’s Ali. Then Sue. Those are my three sisters. And then there’s five of us brothers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did all of you speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎣᎦᏛᏒ -- ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏥᏪᏎᎲ “ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏥᏬᏂᎯ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ ᏲᏁᎦ,’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ”
segments.transliteration: ogadvsv -- sgi tsini,gatsiwesehv “tsalagi, hena, yitsiwonihi, tla yawanv,ta, na yonega,’e gehv”
segments.translation: That’s how we grew up. That’s what I was telling them, “I can speak Cherokee, but I don’t know about English.”

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏗᏥᏁᎸ, ’99 ᏣᏩᏂᎩᏒ Stilwell and ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏁᎯ, ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᎾ, ᎯᎢᎾ ᏧᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏲᏍᏓᏝᏃᎲᎳ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎾᏅ ᎥᎩᏙ Brenda. [To Dianna] You probably know Brenda.
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, squu ditsinelv, ’99 tsawanigisv Stilwell and hesdi, hena, tsi,quisdi, anitsalagi, yanehi, una ditlv, tsigehv yudaha hena, hiina tsutlanohedi yosdatlanohvla, tsalagi, nanv vgido Brenda. [To Dianna] You probably know Brenda.
segments.translation: I went on relocation, I left in ’99. I left Stilwell, and there weren’t any Cherokees living there where I live. Sometimes, I use this [gestures] phone, I call him [Felix] and we speak Cherokee, or my sister, Brenda. [To Dianna] You probably know Brenda.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮳ-ᏣᎳᎩ ᏲᏥᏬᏂᎯ, ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏱᏬᏣ--ᏱᏬᏣᎴᎾ, ᏳᏓᎭ and ᎠᏴ, ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, adopt ᏗᏮᏁᎸ they’re both ᏌᏭ is 19 ᏐᎢ’Ꮕ, 18 ᎠᎬᏱ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏅ is when I got them. ᎾᏅ foster-foster parents ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ, foster-foster parents ᏥᏃᎩᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᎤᏔ,Ꮎ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ Ꮳ-ᏣᎩᏩᏒ and 58 ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: tsa-tsalagi yotsiwonihi, gila yigohida, yonega, yiwotsa--yiwotsalena, yudaha and ayv, tali, anitsutsa, adopt diwvnelv they’re both sawu is 19 soi’nv, 18 agvyi tsuna,denv is when I got them. nanv foster-foster parents agi,sdayvhvsgi, gehv yonega, foster-foster parents tsinogina,dvnv uta,na, gali,tsode tsa-tsagiwasv and 58 diniyotli, tsunilosv una
segments.translation: We all will be talking Cherokee and then sometimes, all of a sudden, we’ll start talking English. I have two adopted boys. They’re both--One is 19 and the other one is 18. I got them when they were born. The foster parents--my wife is a white woman. We became foster parents, I bought a big house. And there’s been 58 children to come through there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah! Foster parents.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏔᎵ - I adopted two of them. ᏌᏭ’Ꭱ-ᏌᏭ’Ꭱ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏐᎢ’Ꮕ, … Sac and Fox. ᎾᏅ Sac and Fox he’s a diesel mechanic.
segments.transliteration: tali - I adopted two of them. sawu’e-sawu’e atsalagi, soi’nv, … Sac and Fox. nanv Sac and Fox he’s a diesel mechanic.
segments.translation: I adopted two of them. One of them is Cherokee and the other one is Sac and Fox. The Sac and Fox boy, he is a diesel mechanic.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏝᏍ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏱᏓᏂᎩᏍᎩ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂ-Sac and Fox? ᎤᎪᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏗᏂᎩᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: tlas adela, yidanigisgi, gohu,sdi, sgina ani-Sac and Fox? ugodi,’e dinigisgi,
segments.translation: Don’t they get a per cap, the Sac and Fox? They get a lot.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: He’s got a lot. He just turned 18. $20,000 Ꮳ-ᏣᏥᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: He’s got a lot. He just turned 18. $20,000 tsa-tsatsinelv
segments.translation: He’s got a lot. He just turned 18. They gave him $20,000.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I know, they get a lot of money.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: And then, ᎾᏅ ᏐᎢ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, “How come I ain’t got no money?” ᏣᏬᏎᎲ “ᎯᏣᎳᎩ,’Ꮫ” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: And then, nanv soi, atsalagi, “How come I ain’t got no money?” tsawosehv “hitsalagi,’dv” tsitsiyohelv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Then the Cherokee boy, “How come I ain’t got no money?” he asked me. “’Cause you’re Cherokee,” I told him. [laughs]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏗᏁᎯ, ᎥᎾ Stilwell ᎥᎾ ᏗᏁᎯ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ,--ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎦᏓᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎾᎥ like nieces and great-nephews and nieces ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏌᏭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv tsi,quisdi, hena, dinehi, vna Stilwell vna dinehi, gohusdi,--gohu,sdi, digadadvne,di nav like nieces and great-nephews and nieces hesdi, sawu tsalagi, gawonisgi, yigi,
segments.translation: Yeah, there’s a lot kinfolks living in Stilwell. Like nieces, and great-nephews and nieces. But not one of them can speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Huh-uh!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: The ones raising them, they weren’t…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: …they weren’t Cherokee speakers.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, … ᎯᎢ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏙ Brenda that’s the only 3. Y’know we grew up with each other.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, tla tsalagi, aniwonisgi, yigi, nigada, … hii hena, udo Brenda that’s the only 3. Y’know we grew up with each other.
segments.translation: They weren’t speakers. This one, and his sister Brenda. They’re the only three. ‘Cause we grew up together.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You all are Cherokee speakers.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏓᎩᎧᎭ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎬᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏯᏃᎵ,Ꭶ, ᎠᏃᎵ,Ꭶ’Ᏺ ᏙᏳ,
segments.transliteration: nanv tali, anitsutsa, dagikaha, tla hena, yigvniwonihi, asenv, yanoli,ga, anoli,ga’yo doyu,
segments.translation: The two boys that I have, they can’t speak, but they understand.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎵᎮᎵᏍᏗ, ᎡᎵᏍᏗ(23:53) ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏙᎲ? ᏣᏃᎵ,Ꭺ ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏅ,ᏗᎰᏍᎪ, ᏙᎨ?
segments.transliteration: ulihelisdi, elisdi osda, dohv? tsanoli,go yaniwonihi, anv,dihosgo, doge?
segments.translation: It’s a good thing that they can understand the language. Do they use it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᏗᏭ Like, ᎠᎭᏫ, ᏥᏔᎩ, ᏥᏍᏆ
segments.transliteration: yaniwonihi, asenv, sdiwu Like, ahawi, tsitagi, tsisqua
segments.translation: They can speak, but it’s just a little. Like Ahaw(i), tsitag(i), tsisgw(a)…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: ….agiyosi.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: “Agiyosi tsitag(a) awaduli”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏣᏂᎶᏍᎬ ᏗᏤᏅᏒ foster ᎾᏍ … ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎵᏙᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏂ-ᎠᏂᎶᏍᎬ ᏴᏓ? ᏧᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏄᎾ,ᏓᎦ,ᏎᏍᏛᎾ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏧᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ … ᎠᎾ,ᏛᏁᎵᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏗᎨᏥᏯᏅᎡᎸ ᏍᎩᎨ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᎶᏍᎨ?
segments.transliteration: na tsadihv diniyotli, tsanilosgv ditsenvsv foster nas … unali,sdanelidohv diniyotli, ani-anilosgv yvda? tsunigayvlige osda, nuna,daga,sesdvna, nowule tsunigayvlige … ana,dvnelisgv yusdi, digetsiyanvelv sgige yusdi anilosge?
segments.translation: What you were talking about, the foster children coming through the house, things happening to them cause the parents weren’t taking care of them. Or the parents were drinking or the other stuff, was that why you all got the kids?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah. … ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, and then, all the tribe. See, where I live, there’s the Kiowa Tribe, Kickapoo, Sac and Fox, and there’s two other tribes…Shawnee. There’s about 6 tribes that conjoins my property. “I’m the only chief in this camp,” ᏥᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏥᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᎾ, … ᎾᏅ Eureka Springs Ꮎ powwow ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎸ and 2-3 years ᎨᎵ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁ(25:23) Cherokee Nation got me sponsors. They said I had the biggest powwow in Arkansas.
segments.transliteration: Yeah. … nigada, hena, anitsalagi, and then, all the tribe. See, where I live, there’s the Kiowa Tribe, Kickapoo, Sac and Fox, and there’s two other tribes…Shawnee. There’s about 6 tribes that conjoins my property. “I’m the only chief in this camp,” tsigatsiyohelv (uniyetsi,sgv) tsitsalagi, hena, … nanv Eureka Springs na powwow tsinawvnelv and 2-3 years geli tsinawadvne Cherokee Nation got me sponsors. They said I had the biggest powwow in Arkansas.
segments.translation: Yeah. All the Cherokees and then all the [other] tribes. See, where I live, there’s the Kiowa Tribe, Kickapoo, Sac and Fox, and there’s two other tribes…Shawnee. There’s about six tribes that conjoin my property. “I’m the only chief in this camp,” I told them. [laughter] Cause I’m Cherokee. And then in Eureka Springs, I put on a powwow. I did for two or three years, I think. Cherokee Nation got me sponsors. They said I had the biggest powwow in Arkansas.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There were all kinds of people who would show up.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Oh, man, we had sponsors: Lowe’s, Home Depot…they were sponsors. They gave me prize money for about $45,000 and I paid the dancers. Ꮎ ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏍᎩᏍᎩ, ᏂᎬ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ,
segments.transliteration: Oh, man, we had sponsors: Lowe’s, Home Depot…they were sponsors. They gave me prize money for about $45,000 and I paid the dancers. na anali,sgisgi, nigv tsunilosv yaniluga,
segments.translation: Oh, man, we had sponsors: Lowe’s, Home Depot…they were sponsors. They gave me prize money for about $45,000 and I paid the dancers. The dancers, they came from all over.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where did you say it was at?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Eureka Springs.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh! I like to go there.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I had 450 acres there. And I sold it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You went to school at Zion, right?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎪᎯᏁᎢ,--ᏍᎪᎯᏁᎢ, ᏥᏩᎩ-- let’s see… Yeah, ᏍᎪᎯᏁᎢ, ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᏃᏭ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ
segments.transliteration: sgohinei,--sgohinei, tsiwagi-- let’s see… Yeah, sgohinei, tsiwagilutsv nowu tsagi,suli,gotsv
segments.translation: I went to the 10th grade, then I quit.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I went to school at Cave Springs.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Cave Springs. ᏣᎳᏍᎦᎸ’Ꭸ ᎨᎮ Cave Springs?
segments.transliteration: Cave Springs. tsalasgalv’ge gehe Cave Springs?
segments.translation: Cave Springs. Did you play ball at Cave Springs?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you play ball at Cave Springs?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Huh-uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᏥᏫᎨᏙᎲ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᏥᏥᎨᎯᏓᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: yudaliha tsiwigedohv awadulihv na anigeyutsa, tsitsigehidasdi
segments.translation: I just went sometimes ‘cause I wanted to chase girls.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Just like a dog. [laughs]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎤᏟ’Ᏼ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏫᎨᏙᎲ it was about ᏑᏓᎵ, 6th grade I guess, ᎠᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ
segments.transliteration: tla utli’yv yigohida, wigedohv it was about sudali, 6th grade I guess, agi,suli,gotsv
segments.translation: It wasn’t very long, I think it was about the sixth grade, I guess, I quit.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ ᏍᎪᎯᏁᎢ, ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ … Daddy ᎮᎾ, -- ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, ᎮᎾ, my dad, he—he couldn’t feed us all. ᏍᎩᏃ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ ᏩᏩᎴᏅᎲ’Ꮕ…
segments.transliteration: ayv’nv sgohinei, tsiwagilutsv … Daddy hena, -- godawasga, hena, my dad, he—he couldn’t feed us all. sgino tsagi,suli,gotsv wawalenvhv’nv…
segments.translation: Me, when I got to the 10th grade, my dad, Godawasg(a), he couldn’t feed us all. That’s why I quit…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: …you started working.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎧᏁᏍᎦ, ᏥᏥᎾᏏᏁᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮎ Bentonville ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏞᎦ, … ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎲ ᏃᏭ - ᏃᏭ truck ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏥᎯᎵᏙᎲ ᏅᏃ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏃᏭ ᏥᏩᏩᎴᏅᎲ
segments.transliteration: kanesga, tsitsinasinesgv nowule na Bentonville tsidagilvwi,sdanelv tlega, … sgina, nigadvnehv nowu - nowu truck tsawalenvhv tsihilidohv nvno osda, nowu tsiwawalenvhv
segments.translation: I was hauling hay and then I went to work in Bentonville for a little while. Just doing this and then I started driving a big truck. That’s when I found a good job.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏣᏙᏓ, ᏙᏳᏛ ᏙᎲ Zion ᏥᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎪᎯᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsadoda, doyudv dohv Zion tsidulvwi,sdanelv gohidi
segments.translation: Your dad worked at Zion for a long time.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: He was a cop.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I remember him working there.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏣᎩᏂᏴᎲ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏚᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗᏭ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎩᏲ’ᎤᏎᎸ Ꭿ-ᎯᎠ ᎤᏙᏓ, ᏣᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ … ᎡᏙᏓ,
segments.transliteration: tsaginiyvhv tsagi,sdunv sawu yuwaga,da, (uyetsi,sgv) agi,sdiwu’dv tsigehv … etsi tsigehv tsogiyo’uselv hi-hia udoda, tsawadvhistanv … edoda,
segments.translation: He caught me and locked me up one time. [laughs] When I was little…we lost my mom. His dad [Leroy] raised me. He was my dad.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: We both lived in the same house for a long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᏍᎪ’Ꮷ ᏫᏍᏓᏓᏅᏖᏝ, ᎤᏍᏗᏭ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎢᏥᏁᎴ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏏᎾ, ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: nowusgo’tsu wisdadanvtetla, usdiwu, gali,tsode itsinele nahiyu tsigesv sina, nowu
segments.translation: When you think about it now, you all probably lived in a small house then like you do now.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: The bathroom was outside.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ Ꮭ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏴᎵᏍᎨ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: nowule nahiyu tsigesv tla usdi gali,tsode yvlisge nigada, hena, ayv nigada, hena,
segments.translation: Back then, you didn’t think you were living in a small house.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ,’Ᏼ ᏓᏤᏢ Ꮓ-ᏃᎦᏛᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎨᎵ
segments.transliteration: doyu hena,’yv datsetlv no-nogadvnv nahiyu tsigehv geli
segments.translation: Really, we were better off that way, back then. I think. Nowadays, it’s remote controls and phones.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎪᎯ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, Ꮎ remote controls and phones - ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ,
segments.transliteration: gohi hena, tsigi, na remote controls and phones - ditlanohedi,
segments.translation: Nowadays, it’s remote controls and phones.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏗᎩᏨᏱ,ᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏕᎨᏅᏒ
segments.transliteration: na tsadihv hesdi, digitsvyi,sdi yigehe degenvsv
segments.translation: You all said, back then we didn’t have electricity.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎪᎯᏅᏏ,(28:54) Ꮎ Ꭰ-ᎠᏟᏍᏓ, ᏥᏚᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: na’dv na gohinvsi, na a-atlisda, tsiduhv edoda, tsigehv
segments.translation: The one you carry, that had kerosene in it. That’s what my dad had.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Kerosene.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: And then if it was cold…the wood stove.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy, ᏍᎩᏛ ᎤᎦᎾᏮ Ꮎ ᎾᏓᏛᏁᎲ … ᏍᏓᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ’Ꮫ … ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏍᏓᏱ, ᏗᏗᏍᏚᎲᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ … ᎾᎯᏳ ᏴᏓ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏰᎾ, ᏙᎯ, ᏗᏓᏍᏚᎰ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏳᏕᏙᏔᏁ ᏃᏭᎴ
segments.transliteration: Boy, sgidv uganawv na nadadvnehv … sdanv,dadisgo’dv … hesdi, sdayi, didisduhvsgv, yigehe galohisdi … nahiyu yvda digaduhv yena, dohi, didasduho asenv, tla gilo ilvhiyu gohusdi, yudedotane nowule
segments.translation: Boy, that really warmed you up. You all remember…they didn’t lock their doors. Like when we went to the store, we didn’t lock our door. But people never messed with anything.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Nowadays, they break a window and crawl in.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᎯᎳ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏛᏂᏩᏛᎯ ᏫᏄᏅᏁ,Ꮧ ᏭᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᎨᏍᏗ … ᏃᏭᎴᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏓᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎨᏱ ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎦᏙ ᎠᎹ, ᎠᏟᏍᏛ ᎠᎫᎩᏍᏗ’,Ꮕ ᏥᎦᎶ ᎩᎶ ᏳᎶᏌ, Ᏼ-ᏴᏗᏔ, ᏃᏭᎴ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, squu’dv hila sdayi gohusdi, dvniwadvhi winunvne,di wuniyvsdi doyu, una,duligesdi … nowulenv squu sdanv,dadiho’dv squu gogeyi yigi, doyi ditlv tsigado ama, atlisdv agugisdi’,nv tsigalo gilo yulosa, yv-yvdita, nowule
segments.translation: Yeah, that, too, they’re going to find a way to get in. And you all remember, too, during the summer there would be a bucket of water and a dipper. When somebody came or walked by, they would get a drink of water.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: The dippers were long.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But that doesn’t happen today, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏛ’Ᏺ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂ--ᎤᏂᏁᎫᏥᏓ, ᏃᏭ ᏴᏫ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏴ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ Oklahoma City ᏫᎨᏙᎰ … ᏌᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, parking lot Ꮵ-ᏥᎦᎢᏒ ᎤᎾ Quail Springs Mall was where I was going, and then ᎠᏂᎬᎿᎨ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ ᏦᎢ ᎾᏂᎥ
segments.transliteration: igadv’yo tsiquisdi, uni--uninegutsida, nowu yvwi, gohi tsigi, ayv hena, nigohilv Oklahoma City wigedoho … sawu’nv, yuwaga,da, parking lot tsi-tsigaisv una Quail Springs Mall was where I was going, and then anigvhnage tsunilutsv tsoi naniv
segments.translation: There’s too many mean people today. I go to Oklahoma City all the time. One time I was coming through the parking lot at Quail Springs Mall was where I was going, and then three black people came.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Like you.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏂᎯ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᎾ, Ꮎ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏯᏪᎾ, ᎦᎶᏇ ᎠᏭᏱᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᎶᏇ … Ꮎ ᎦᎶᏇ ᏣᎩᎴᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏛᎩ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏴᏅ(30:48)
segments.transliteration: nihi yusdi, tsigehv … nigohilv hena, na ‘lvtlv yawena, galoque awuyisgo sgina, tsagi,sdelvhv na galoque … na galoque tsagilesv nowule dvgi, yusdi tsuna,daniyvnv
segments.translation: They were like you. When I go somewhere I always carry a gun. That’s what helped me, the gun. When I pulled out the gun, they took off like flies.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: They probably would’ve beat you up, if you didn’t have the gun.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They would’ve stole from you.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I would’ve used my karate and whupped them all. [laughs]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎪᎳ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏙᏱ, ᎣᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗᏍᎬ, ᎾᏅ ᏥᏍᏚ, ᏥᏏᏙᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ (…) ᎾᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏑᏍᏗ, ᏱᎪᏢᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ gravy soup ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎪᏢᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: gola hena, yigi, doyu hena,’yo osda, doyi, odanv,dv tsigehv tsotsiyotli, tsigehv gola yigi, nigali,sdodisgv, nanv tsisdu, tsisidohi tsigehv (…) nanv etsi tsigehv na ususdi, yigotlvna, tsigehv gravy soup sgina yigotlvna, tsigehv
segments.translation: When it was winter and we were kids, we were feeling good. Because the rabbits, we would go look for them. Mom would make gravy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏌᎵᎶ,’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: salilo,’dv squu doyu utedi, tsigehv dohv?
segments.translation: Squirrel was really good, too, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏳᏚᎵᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏳᏚᎵᎮ ᎦᎶᏇ ᎣᎬᏛᏗ ᏅᏲ Ꮵ-ᏥᏙᏨᏗᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: hesdi, yudulihe edoda, tsigehv hesdi yudulihe galoque ogvdvdi nvyo tsi-tsidotsvdisgv
segments.translation: Our dad didn’t want us using a gun, we had to use rocks.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, if we saw a squirrel, [we killed it.]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You all were dropping them. [The squirrels]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: We’d throw the rocks out and ᏲᏨᏂᎦ,
segments.transliteration: We’d throw the rocks out and yotsvniga,
segments.translation: We’d throw the rocks and we’d hit them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What did your dad say when you brought them?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: “Ꭷ! ᏗᏗᏯᎩ!” – “ᎭᏓᏍᏓᏴᎭ ᏂᎯ, ᎯᎨᏯ!” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ ᎠᎩᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: “ka! didiyagi!” – “hadasdayvha nihi, higeya!” agohelv agitsi tsigehv
segments.translation: “OK. Let’s eat them!” – “Woman, you cook it!” he’d tell our mom.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did you all bring a lot of them?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎯᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏃᏥ’Ꭱ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏢ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᎭᏫᏅ, ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ they was just everywhere. Nobody owned them. We’d just go get the…
segments.transliteration: vv hisgi’e notsi’e otsatlanvtlv nigada, gehv ahawinv, nahiyu’e squu tsigehv na siqua they was just everywhere. Nobody owned them. We’d just go get the…
segments.translation: There were five of us brothers. And then deer. And then, back then pigs, they was just everywhere. Nobody owned them. We’d just go get the…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did all of y’all help each other?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ,-- Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ, ᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏧᏃᎭᎴᏒ ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏥᏚᏃᏢ ᏏᏆ, “What’re you gonna do? I’m not gonna fix them, I’ll be here all week,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎩᎶ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ ᏥᏫ,ᏚᏁᏎ ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏥᏚᏃᏢ ᏏᏆ, … Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏁᎯ, ᎢᎾ
segments.transliteration: na atsutsa, agikaha,-- na atsutsa, agikaha, ganohalidohi, hena, ilvsgi, nusv tsigehv … tsunohalesv sudali, tsidunotlv siqua, “What’re you gonna do? I’m not gonna fix them, I’ll be here all week,” tsitsiyohelv … asenv, gilo tsunilutsv tsiwi,dunese sudali, tsidunotlv siqua, … tsi,quisdi, hena, anehi, ina
segments.translation: The boy I have-- The boy I have, he’s a hunter. Not long ago, he went hunting and he brought in six pigs. “What’re you gonna do? I’m not going to fix them, I’ll be here all week,” I told him. But somebody came and took the pigs. He brought in six pigs. There are a lot of them there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Are they good to eat?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏗᏭ ᏱᎩ, ᎾᏅ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᏥᎩ, Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏒᎪ
segments.transliteration: usdiwu yigi, nanv tsuna,tana, tsigi, na anisvgo
segments.translation: When they’re small. If they’re big, they smell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏌᏭ ᏤᎲ Kenwood Woody Hair ᏧᏙᎢᏛ, … ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ, ᏏᏆ, ᏳᏢ, Ꮎ ᎠᎹ, ᏥᏩᏑᏴᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ, ᎡᏧᎳ ᏱᏗᎬᏂᏍᏗᎰ ᏌᏭ ... ᏧᎳᏍᎩ, … ᎣᏍᏛ’Ꮕ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏴᏕᎳᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏎᏅ ᏣᏗ ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, “ᏧᏂᏍᏗᏭ” ᏣᏗᎰ ‘Ꮫ “ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ,” ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ “ᏧᎾ,ᏔᏂ’Ꮓ ᏍᏓᏱ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ, ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ”
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv sawu tsehv Kenwood Woody Hair tsudoidv, … inage ehi, siqua, yutlv, na ama, tsiwasuyvsgv nowu osda, yuwvnistanv, etsula yidigvnisdiho sawu ... tsulasgi, … osdv’nv agisdi, tsigehv tla howa yvdelaho tsigehv … asenv tsadi doyu, hena, “tsunisdiwu” tsadiho ‘dv “osda, digayesdi,” nowule squu “tsuna,tani’no sdayi’dv nowu, digayesdi, gehv”
segments.translation: There was one in Kenwood, his name was Woody Hair. When he killed a wild pig, he would add salt when he cooked it. He would cook both of them, in one big pot. It was good to eat, you couldn’t tell. Like you said, he would say, “The little ones are good to eat.” But the older/bigger ones are hard to eat.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do they skin them? Or what do they do?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎢᏡ,Ꭼ ᏓᎾ,ᏛᏍᎪ then they scrape it. They skin it, they take the whole skin off.
segments.transliteration: na itlu,gv dana,dvsgo then they scrape it. They skin it, they take the whole skin off.
segments.translation: They hang them on a tree, they don’t do scraping, they just take the skin off while they’re hanging up there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’ᎡᏲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏗᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ scrape ᏥᏂ,ᏙᏨᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’eyo edoda, dihi tsigehv na scrape tsini,dotsvnehv
segments.translation: When my dad used to kill hogs, we had to scrape them.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏛᏁᎲ we put them in hot water.
segments.transliteration: eduda, squu sgi tsinadvnehv we put them in hot water.
segments.translation: Our grandpa had us doing that, too. We put them in hot water.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ ᏥᏓ-ᏓᏂᏢᏍᎬ ᏏᏆ, ᎾᏅ … ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏥᏄᏅᏁ Ꮎ ᏓᏂᏍᏚᏟᎲ ᎾᏅ ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮎ
segments.transliteration: nahena tsida-danitlvsgv siqua, nanv … uganawa tsinunvne na danisdutlihv nanv nowule na
segments.translation: They would put the hogs on the table and then warm the water they would pour the water on them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, they would pour hot water on them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ … ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎬᏁᎸ’Ꮓ ᎤᏔᎾ, barrel *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏄᏮᏅ ᎤᏗᏞᎬ ᏥᎨᎰ’Ꮓ ᎠᎹ, ᎾᏅ ᏧᎵ,ᏦᏗ, ᏦᏍᏗᎸᏍᎪ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏞᎦ, ᏃᏭᏅ ᎪᎯᏴ’Ꮓ ᏱᏬᏍᏗᎴᏍᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᎢᏭ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎦᎵᎲ’Ꮓ … ᏙᏳ’ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏂᏏᎾᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᎾ,ᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎠᎭᏫ, ᏧᏂᏅᎦᎸᏍᏗᎲ(34:49) ᏞᎦᏭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏂᎯᎵᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sawu yuwaga,da, tsitsisdelihv … osda, nigvnelv’no utana, barrel *hii* tsinuwvnv uditlegv tsigeho’no ama, nanv tsuli,tsodi, tsosdilvsgo nowule tlega, nowunv gohiyv’no yiwosdilesga, tsigehv nowu sginana nowu, aiwu osdinegalihv’no … doyu’hena, igada, hena, doyu, anisinasdi, gehv sgina yuna,dvne,di ahawi, tsuninvgalvsdihv tlegawu squu yanihilida, tsigehv
segments.translation: I helped one time, to fix a hog, he was using a big barrel and he had it like this [gestures]. The water was real hot and we put it in there for awhile. Then we took it out and then we scraped it. There were some people who were real good at it. It would take them just a little while to fix it.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏣᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏧᎩᏨᏓᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏙᏥᏰᏍᎬ ᎠᏣᏗ, ᎠᎹᏱ ᎾᎥᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: atsadi hena, nigohilv’dv tsugitsvdawu yusdi, dotsiyesgv atsadi, amayi navwu tsigehv
segments.translation: We always ate fish, just about every day. There was a creek nearby.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏃ ᏴᏓ … ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ, Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏒᎩ ᏱᎩ, ᏝᏓᏱᏓᏱ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎬ’Ꭸ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: nano yvda … inage ehi, na’dv svgi yigi, tladayidayi’le yigi, itsigisgv’ge gehe?
segments.translation: How about the wild onions? Or the poke salad? Did you all eat those?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Wild onion, yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᏣᎳᎩ, Ꮎ Watercress.
segments.transliteration: nanv tla yawanv,ta, dudov tsalagi, na Watercress.
segments.translation: And then, I don’t know what to call it in Cherokee, but Watercress.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They call it Atsil(a).

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, I like that.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ᏺ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ ᎠᏴ -- ‘Ꮲ ᎡᎯᏍ Ꮟ Watercress?
segments.transliteration: sgi’yo agilvquo,di ayv -- ‘tlv ehis si Watercress?
segments.translation: That’s what I like. Does it still grow?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᎹᏱ ᎠᏥᎳ, ᎤᏚᏅ, ᎨᎵ ᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏛᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: amayi atsila, udunv, geli danoheho sgina amayi hena, tsadvsgo
segments.translation: Amayi Atsil(a) Udun(v) they call it ‘cause it grows in the water.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏱᎦᏅᎪᎪ ‘Ꮲ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏤᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: nowule yudaha yiganvgogo ‘tlv tsi,quisdi, tsehv sgina
segments.translation: Yeah, or at a spring, there’ll be a lot growing.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: It’s real good to eat.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what we grew up with.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮓ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᏣᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ…
segments.transliteration: nowule’no tsisdvni nowule tsadisgv atsadi, nowule…
segments.translation: Yeah, and then there’s crawdads and, like you said, fish.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎧᏄᎾ … … ᏳᏓᎭ ᏓᎦ,Ꮟ, ᏣᏂᏒᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏅ, I didn’t try it. ᏥᏥᏍᎦᏰᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: kanuna … … yudaha daga,si, tsanisvsgv asenv, I didn’t try it. tsitsisgayehv sgina agisdi
segments.translation: And bullfrogs. And then sometimes they’d cook up turtle, but I didn’t try it. I was too scared to eat it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎥᎩᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏁᎸ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏧᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᏏᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏯᎩᎨ ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ ᏝᏩᏅ,Ꮦ ᎦᏳᏓᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏭ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᏯᎩᎨ
segments.transliteration: na’e vgido tsigehv aninelv, sawu yuwaga,da, sgi yusdi, tsuwvnistanv osiwu tsigehv agisdi, asenv, tla utli iga yagige doyu’nv tlawanv,te gayudadvne,di nowu ugodi, yagige
segments.translation: One time, my late sister, her husband cooked it. It was good to eat, but I didn’t eat too much. I didn’t know how it would affect me if I had eaten a lot of it.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏥᏍᏛᎾ,’Ꭱ ᏱᏙᎩᏯᎴᏌ, ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏅᏲ ᎮᎾ, ᏓᎲ ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏂᏯᎠ, ᏙᏥᏂᏱᏍᎬ--ᏙᏥᏂᏱᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ Ꮩ’ᎢᏃᏢ’Ꮓ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ “ᎠᎭᏂ--ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꭱ ᏕᎬᏂᏍᏕ Ꮎ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ’Ꮕ, ᎦᏚ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎢᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎭ!” ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎾ ᏱᏥᏙᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ “’ᏙᎲᏅ ᎠᏂᎩᎦᎨ ᏥᎩ,? ᏞᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏂᎩᎦᎨ--“
segments.transliteration: tsisdvna,’e yidogiyalesa, edoda, tsigehv uyo tsigehv nvyo hena, dahv hawini, ditlv, aniyaa, dotsiniyisgv--dotsiniyisgv nowu do’inotlv’no etsi tsigehv nowu “ahani--ahani,’e degvnisde na tsisdvna, ahani’nv, gadu nigada, itsali,sdayvha!” ayv’nv agi,sdi tsigehv ina yitsidoga, tsigehv “’dohvnv anigigage tsigi,? tlesdi,’e anigigage--“
segments.translation: When we’d go look for crawdads, my father and Uyo, they [crawdads] were under rocks. And we caught them. Then when we brought them home, Mom would cook them and say “Here are the crawdads I cooked, and here’s the bread. You all eat.” I was little, and I was standing there, “Why are they red? They weren’t red when I caught them.”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They weren’t red when you all caught them.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: They weren’t red when I caught them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᏄᏍᏗ, Ꭼ,ᏗᎮ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ? ᎠᏗᏍ Ꭼ,ᏔᏅ ᏙᎨ?
segments.transliteration: ‘do nusdi, gv,dihe adasdayv,di? adis gv,tanv doge?
segments.translation: What kind of stove was she using? Wood or what?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᏓ - ᎠᏓ ᏗᎬ,ᏙᏗ ᎥᎥ Ꮎ
segments.transliteration: vv na ada - ada digv,dodi vv na
segments.translation: A wood stove.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: It was real small.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: “ᎠᏓ’Ꮫ ᏫᏘᏍᎷᏯ! Ꮎ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏓᎦᏓᏍᏓᏴᏂ,” ᏯᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᏱ y’know … ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᎲᏛ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: “ada’dv witisluya! na adasdayv,di dagadasdayvni,” yadi, tsigehv doyi y’know … adasdayv,di dihvdv,di
segments.translation: “Go cut wood! I’m going to cook,” she’d say. I would go cut them into the size you put into the stove.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏴᏫ, ᏗᎬᏩᏛᎯᏓᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎨᏱ ᏱᎩ, ᏂᏙᏣᏕᏠ;ᏆᏍᎬᎾ ᏱᎩ, ᎡᏥ Ꮎ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎥᎩᏙ … ᏙᏣᏓᏩᏛᎮᎬ ‘Ꮲ ᏔᎵᎭ - ᏦᎢᎭ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏳᏒ ᏱᏬᏤ--ᏱᏬᏤᏙᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏍᎦ,ᏍᎨ
segments.transliteration: na’e squu etiyv tsigehv yvwi, digvwadvhidasdi, tsigehv gogeyi yigi, nidotsadetlo;quasgvna yigi, etsi na uwasa, dogina,dvhistanv vgido … dotsadawadvhegv ‘tlv taliha - tsoiha’le yigi, yusv yiwotse--yiwotsedohv nahiyu tsigehv tla yana,dasga,sge
segments.translation: A long time ago, people would go visit one another. In the summer, when we weren’t in school. My mom raised me and my sister by herself. We would go visit and stay for two or three nights. They didn’t get tired of us.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Lyon Switch ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏬᏥᏁᎸ ᏞᎦ, … ᎾᏅ Sanders Flat…
segments.transliteration: Lyon Switch hena, squu tsiwotsinelv tlega, … nanv Sanders Flat…
segments.translation: We lived in Lyon Switch for a while. Around Sanders Flat…

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏛᏒ ᎯᎢ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏙᏓ, ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ
segments.transliteration: nigada,’dv etsulaha yusdi, tsogina,dvsv hii, hena, udoda, awadvhistanv etsi tsigehv tsogiyohuselv
segments.translation: We grew up together. His dad raised me, because my mom died.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I was always mad at him. [laughs]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You were fed up with him. [laughs]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: When I’d turn around, he’d be right there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: “He’s following me around,” you thought.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎣᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ’Ꮕ, ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏭᎦ,ᏔᎲᏌ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᎪᏍᏗ, ᏱᏥᎳᏴᎾ,(38:23)
segments.transliteration: otsali,sdayvhvsgv’nv, yigi, yiwuga,tahvsa, nahiyu gosdi, yitsilayvna,
segments.translation: When we were eating, when he’d turn around, I would take something from his plate.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: That’s why I’m skinny.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, … ᏃᏭᎴ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎡᏥ ᎤᏠᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏬᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏓ, ᎪᏙᏗ ᎠᏓ-ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎤᏩᎧᎲ … ᏗᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏓᏭ,’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮟ’Ᏺ ᏓᏝ’Ꭱ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏳᏩᏃᏒᎭ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎣᏍᏓ, (…)[38:57] ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎪᎳ,--ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ, … ᏃᏭ ᏳᏓᏍᏓᏴᎾ, Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᎤᎦᎾᏮ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏙᏳ,Ꮂ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᎦ,ᏙᎲᏒ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎯ?
segments.transliteration: nahena, … nowule ganvdadiho sawu yuwaga,da, etsi utlogi, tsigehv wotsiwa,dvhidolv sgina, ada, gododi ada-adasdayv,di uwakahv … didasdayv,di ditlv, gadawu,’e tsigehv si’yo datla’e nowule yuwanosvha, nowule osda, (…)[38:57] tsigehv nowule gola,--gola yigi, … nowu yudasdayvna, na’dv squu gadohi, uganawv tsigehv … doyu,hv sgi tsinusdv nahiyu tsigehv tla yawanv,ta, sgi yusdi sdiga,dohvsv yigi nihi?
segments.translation: I remember, one time we went to visit my mother’s aunt. She had a wood stove. Where she cooked, the floor was just dirt. When she swept, it was good. And then in the winter time, when she cooked the ground was warm. That’s how it used to be, I don’t know if you all have lived that way?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I remember that a little bit.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, … ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ and then Ꮎ … ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ’Ꮓ ᏍᎩ ᏦᎩ-- ᏧᏂᏝᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏦᏥᏘᏲᎯᎲ Ꮎ party line.
segments.transliteration: sdigida, … ganvdadihv yudaha and then na … ditlanohedi’no sgi tsogi-- tsunitlanv una gali,tsode nigohilv’dv tsotsitiyohihv na party line.
segments.translation: I remember a little, sometimes. And then I remember we got the telephone in the house. We used to argue with the people on the party line.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how it was, wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏦᏍᏓᏝᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꮎ … ᎠᎩ,ᏐᎮᎲ’Ꮕ -- I tied the line up.
segments.transliteration: nigohilv’dv tsosdatlanohesgv na … agi,sohehv’nv -- I tied the line up.
segments.translation: She and I were always talking. Then they’d get onto me. I was tying up the line.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They got onto you. [laughs]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I didn’t care that they got onto me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎡᏘ’Ᏼ party line.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv sgi tsinusdv eti’yv party line.
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how it was a long time ago, a party line.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It was real annoying.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮧ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ T.V. you had to get up and turn the channel. Black and white’Ꮕ
segments.transliteration: uneli,di, hena, tsigehv nowu’nv T.V. you had to get up and turn the channel. Black and white’nv
segments.translation: Yeah, it was bothersome. And then T.V. you had to get up to turn the channel. And it was black and white.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ The 3 Stooges’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏭ’Ꮫ ᏥᎦᏛ
segments.transliteration: nigohilv’dv The 3 Stooges’dv tsigehv awu’dv tsigadv
segments.translation: Yeah, it was always The Three Stooges. The T.V. was hanging just right there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏃ’Ꮂ radio? ‘Ꮩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎢᏥᎮ Ꮎ radio?
segments.transliteration: nano’hv radio? ‘do yusdi itsihe na radio?
segments.translation: How about the radio? What kind did you all have?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ console record player ᎤᏔᎾ, ᏱᎩᏗ,
segments.transliteration: na console record player utana, yigidi,
segments.translation: That console record player. It’s big.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏗᏭ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, … Ꮎ ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏗᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ Ꮎ
segments.transliteration: usdiwu’dv yusdi, … na digali,disdi tsigeho na
segments.translation: It was little, the kind you put [a VHS/Cassette tape] in.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Cassette.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎦᎵ,ᏗᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎾᏅ, T.V. ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᏴᎳᏛᏍᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏁᎦ, y’know … y’know you just … ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᏲᏣᏲᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏂᏫᏗᎲ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎩᎶ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᏂᏅᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv gohusdi gali,disdi, yusdi tsigehv nowule usdi nowule … sgiwu’dv yusdi nanv, T.V. gehv adayvladvsgi, gehv usdi tsigehv unega, y’know … y’know you just … yudaliha yotsayogv nowule tsaniwidihv ‘lvtlv gilo osda daninvnehv
segments.translation: Yeah, you had to put something in. It was little, that’s what we had. And then about the T.V., it was little, too. It was real small and white. Sometimes it would break and they would take it somewhere to have it fixed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ tubes ᏥᏕᎨᏙ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᏣᏂᏩᏘᏍᎪ ᏄᏓᎴ tube ᏧᏅᏁᏗ
segments.transliteration: na’dv tubes tsidegedo oni, ditlv, eliwu tsaniwatisgo nudale tube tsunvnedi
segments.translation: There were like ‘tubes’ in the back. And they would find new ones and put them in to fix it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: When it broke, it just went off.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, it went to sleep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That was sad. [laughs] They were playing music, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ, ᎾᏃ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏛᏂ ᏗᏣᎦ,ᏙᏍᏗᏍᎬ, ᏝᎨ? Television-Ꭲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv sgi tsinusdv nahiyu ganvdadisgo squu ayv, nano dina,dadvni ditsaga,dosdisgv, tlage? Television-i
segments.translation: Yeah, really, that’s how it was back then. I remember it, too. Did you all watch cartoons on T.V.?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎡᏚᏥ, ᎠᏂᏦᎢᎭ ᎾᏂᎥ ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᎠᏳᏁᎦ, no, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮫ --no, ᎠᏳᏁᎦ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᏧᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᎤᏂ,Ꮵ *ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ* ᏱᎦᏘ, ᏦᏣᎯᎵᏐ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏛᏂ’ᏛᏃ ᏫᏙᏣᎦ,ᏙᏛ ᎤᎾᎾ “Spider-Web” ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᏤᎲ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏂᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, edutsi, anitsoiha naniv squu’dv ayunega, no, atsalagi’dv --no, ayunega’dv tsigehv asenv atsalagi, usdayvhvsgi, tsigehv sgiyusdi, tsuhv tsadihv squu’dv uni,tsi *hii’dv* yigati, tsotsahiliso dina,dadvni’dvno widotsaga,dodv unana “Spider-Web” tsudoida, tsehv doyu unilvquo,di, tsigehv sgina
segments.translation: My uncles, there were three of them. One was a white man and had a Cherokee wife. And that’s what he had, the T.V. you mentioned. We used to walk through snow this [gestures] tall to go watch cartoons on their T.V.. It was called “Spider Web.” They really liked that back then.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Spider-Man.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ ᏂᎯ ᎣᏍᏛ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᏴ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv aseno tla yawanv,ta, sdelisgv nihi osdv nogadvnv gelisgo ayv, nahiyu tsigesv
segments.translation: Yeah, really, but I don’t know what you all think about it, but I think we were living real well back then.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, back then.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’ᏛᏲ not--ᎪᎯ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, it’s a lot of stress. These Ꮎ electronics ᎾᏅ technology, it’s just out of hand.
segments.transliteration: doyu’dvyo not--gohi hena, tsigi, it’s a lot of stress. These na electronics nanv technology, it’s just out of hand.
segments.translation: Really though, today it’s a lot of stress. These electronics. This technology, it’s just out of hand.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏲᏟ, ᏱᎪᎥ ᎠᎢᏭ ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎵᏙᎯ, ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ … ᏳᏗᏍᎬ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎩᎶ ᎠᎢᏒ ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏱᎪᎥ ᏏᏛ Ꮟ ᎠᎢ ᏂᏙᎬᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv nowu squu ayotli, yigov aiwu nidegvnelidohi, ditlanohedi … yudisgv, nowule squu gilo aisv nvnohi, yigov sidv si ai nidogvnehv
segments.translation: Yeah, when you see a child, they will be messing with a phone, with their head down. And also, when you see somebody walking down the road, they are doing the same thing.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Even when they’re driving.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏥᏕᎦᏘᏂᏙᎲ Ꮎ baseball, I was the coach. ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎯᎳ--Anybody got the time?” ᏣᏩᏛᏅ “Anybody know what time it is?” ᏂᎦᏓ, cellphones ᏥᏚᏂᎴᏒ
segments.transliteration: nanv tsuni,sdi diniyotli, tsidegatinidohv na baseball, I was the coach. tsuni,sdi tsigehv “hila--Anybody got the time?” tsawadvnv “Anybody know what time it is?” nigada, cellphones tsidunilesv
segments.translation: I was coaching a little league baseball team. They were small. One time I said, “Does anybody got the time?” And they all pulled out their cellphones. [laughs]
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ “What—what does this word mean?” ᏴᏓ ᎩᎳᏭ’Ꮫ ᏓᏂᎴᎢ ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv nowule … nowule squu “What—what does this word mean?” yvda gilawu’dv danilei ditlanohedi
segments.translation: And also, someone will ask “What does this word mean?” Then they take out their cellphone.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: They’ll look it up.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏩᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰ ᎦᏓ,Ꭷ ᏍᎩᎾ … ᎢᏴ ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ, ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nowule wana,delaho gada,ka sgina … iyv dudalehnada, nowu
segments.translation: Yeah, then they’ll figure out what it means. It’s real different nowadays.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏙᏳ Ꮎ old days ᏙᎲ ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏥ--if you think about it, I think it was better.
segments.transliteration: doyu na old days dohv yigi, yitsi--if you think about it, I think it was better.
segments.translation: Really, the old days, when you think about it. I think it was better.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Y’know that, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎠᏜ ᏥᏯᏏᏙᎢᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: Y’know that, nigohilv’dv na adla tsiyasidoidohv
segments.translation: I used to always push around a tire.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏍ ᏣᏁᎶ,ᏙᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ? ᏝᎨ ᏐᎢ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏐᎢ, ᎢᏦᏢᏍᎨ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᏣᏁᎶ,ᏙᏗ,? ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꭸ?
segments.transliteration: sgis tsanelo,dodi, gehv nahiyu? tlage soi, gohusdi, soi, itsotlvsge gohu,sdi, ditsanelo,dodi,? sgiwu’ge?
segments.translation: That was your toy back then? You all didn’t make anything else to play with, or was that it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Huh uh. Ꭺ-ᎪᎯᏴ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎩ,’Ᏺ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏱᎪᏢᎾ, ᏃᏭ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎭᏰᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮎ tombstones ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. go-gohiyv’nv, tsigi,’yo yusdiwu gehv yigotlvna, nowu gohi tsigi, hayeli,sdi degotlvsgo nowule na tombstones degotlvsgo
segments.translation: Uh-uh. Nowadays, I can make anything. I make knives and tombstones.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? Do you sell them?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
