segments.text: Yeah, I got a-- ᏥᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏚᎾ,ᏚᎵ ᏴᏫ, and I don’t have enough help. ᎾᏅ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎡᎵᏏᏅ, and my two uncles. They have no markers on the graves. And I made crosses for them. [To Felix] Let’s see, next month-Ꮫ ᏙᏓᏗᏢᏂ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, I got a-- tsiquisdi, hena, duna,duli yvwi, and I don’t have enough help. nanv eduda, elisinv, and my two uncles. They have no markers on the graves. And I made crosses for them. [To Felix] Let’s see, next month-dv dodaditlvni dohv?
segments.translation: Yeah. --There’s a lot of people who want them. But I don’t have enough help. My grandpa and my grandmother, then my two uncles. They don’t have gravemarkers. I made crosses for them. [To Felix] Let’s see, we’ll have decoration next month?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Uh-huh. Next month is May, right?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah. And I made crosses for them.
segments.transliteration: Yeah. And I made crosses for them.
segments.translation: Yeah. And I made crosses for them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Flute Springs.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where is it at? Flute Springs?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Flute Springs.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, that’s where they’re at. Your daddy is in Fairfield, ᎥᎾᎧ ᎤᎾ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, that’s where they’re at. Your daddy is in Fairfield, vnaka una?
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s where they’re at. Your daddy is in Fairfield, right?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Your dad.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Fairfield.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Huh uh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Fairfield. That’s where Godawasg(a) is buried.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, he’s buried there.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᎤᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏂᏌᎲ ᎧᎵ,ᏍᏓᏯ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎩᎵᏏ …
segments.transliteration: nanv utanida, tsosdadanvtli, una squu ganisahv kali,sdaya’nv, agilisi …
segments.translation: My oldest brother, too, that’s where he’s buried. And then Kal(i)sday(a) and my grandma…

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: …Flute Springs…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: …my mom, [she’s buried at] Flute Springs.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ ᏧᎯᎶᏢ Ꮎ 2020 ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᏴᏫ ᏕᎦᎷᎦ, ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏍᏊ ᏕᎦᎷᎦ, ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: nahena tsuhilotlv na 2020 tsiquisdosv yvwi degaluga, tsiquisdosv anitsalagi, squu degaluga, sgina
segments.translation: When the disease came in 2020, man, there were a lot of people that it killed. And there were a lot of Cherokees that we lost.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: That Covid[-19?]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎬ’ᏛᎲ ᎡᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎲ? ᏙᎲ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏎ ᎠᏂᏳᏁᎦ’Ꭱ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓ, ᏴᏫ, ᏚᏘᏅᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: nigv’dvhv ehe sgina dohv? dohv squu tla squu doyu, anitsalagiwu iga unanigise aniyunega’e tsudalenvda, yvwi, dutinvstanv sgina
segments.translation: Yeah, it was all over. It wasn’t just Cherokees that died, but it took out a lot of whites and other peoples.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᏍᎩ ᏧᏢ … ᏧᏓ--ᏧᏓᏂᎶᏒ 2 weeks ᏥᏭᏲᎱᏒ
segments.transliteration: nanv utanida, tsosdadanvtli, sgi tsutlv … tsuda--tsudanilosv 2 weeks tsiwuyohusv
segments.translation: That’s what got him, my older brother. When he got sick, it took two weeks for him to pass.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Janice ᎠᏂᏁᎳ, Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏳᏓᎭ ᏣᏁᏙᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᎯᏳ-- Janice’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎭᎴ ᏄᏅᏍᏔᏅ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Janice aninela, na’e edoda, yudaha tsanedoho sgina disdadanvtli, sgina, nahiyu-- Janice’dv squu hale nunvstanv dohv?
segments.translation: Janice and her husband, they came to visit my dad sometimes. That brother of yours--and it almost got Janice, too.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Me too!

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: You [Leroy] almost died, too!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Nine-nine days ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᎾ Stillwater Hospital. Stillwater. And 9 days, and 3 days Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮦ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏂᏙᎲ … ᎾᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ’Ꮕ ᏧᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᏥᏫ,ᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᎤᏂᏴᏟᏢ … ᎭᎴ ᎠᎩᎵᏬᏨ’Ᏺ
segments.transliteration: Nine-nine days tsinawali,stanv una Stillwater Hospital. Stillwater. And 9 days, and 3 days tla yawanv,te nigali,sdanidohv … nanv etsi tsosdadanvtli’nv tsuniyohusv tsiwi,gatsigov uniyvtlitlv … hale agiliwotsv’yo
segments.translation: I was in the hospital at Stillwater for nine days. And three of those days, I don’t remember anything. Then I saw my mom and my brother, they had both already passed. But they came into my room. I almost died then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᏅ ᎠᏥᏃᏎᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ, Ꮎ ᏗᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, “’ᎸᏢ ᏫᏍᎩ,ᏔᏂᏙᎸᎢ ᎭᎴ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ Janice ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, “ᎲᏩ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ “Ꮎ kitchen-Ꭲ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏍᏔᏅ” (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: sgidvnv atsinosehe edoda, na disdadanvtli, “’lvtlv wisgi,tanidolvi hale awedolv nigehvna,” awohelv Janice tsadihv usdayvhvsgi, “hvwa” tsiyohelv tsadihv “na kitchen-i witsiyatistanv” (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: That’s what your brother was telling my dad: He said, “Take me somewhere where I’ve never been!” she [Janice] told me. “Alright,” I told her. “So I took her into the kitchen!” [laughs]
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “Here it is!” I told her, [he said.] She thought it was funny.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎾ--ᎥᎾ ᏫᏓᎨᏙᎵ, Janice ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏓᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎵ, ᏞᎦ,
segments.transliteration: vna--vna widagedoli, Janice tsuwenvhv datsiwa,dvhidoli, tlega,
segments.translation: That’s where I’m going, to Janice’s house, to visit her.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where did you say you lived?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Oklahoma City. A little ways out of OKC, it’s called Wellston. Wellston ᎤᎾ ᏥᏁᎳ, But I’m just like 20 minutes to OKC.
segments.transliteration: Oklahoma City. A little ways out of OKC, it’s called Wellston. Wellston una tsinela, But I’m just like 20 minutes to OKC.
segments.translation: Oklahoma City. A little ways out of OKC, Wellston. That’s where I live, but I’m just about 20 minutes from OKC.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ! ᎭᎴ’Ꭸ ᏣᏃᎴᏔᏅ ᏔᎵᎭ ᏄᏒ ᏥᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: o! hale’ge tsanoletanv taliha nusv tsigesv
segments.translation: Oh! Did you almost get blown away two nights ago?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, a tornado went by.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ … Gopher ᏣᏩᏤᎸᏅ ᎦᏁᎵᏗᎲ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᏥᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: ayv’nv … Gopher tsawatselvnv ganelidihv gadohi, tsiwagiyvtlv una
segments.translation: I acted like I was a gopher, I went underground.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏦᎢᏭ’Ꭱ ᎾᏂᎥ ᏃᏭ ᎯᎢᎾ [Leroy and ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏝ] ᎯᎢ ᎨᎲ Brenda ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ’Ꮕ, George … ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏁᎳ, ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ
segments.transliteration: tsoiwu’e naniv nowu hiina [Leroy and anatlanvtla] hii gehv Brenda dina,danvtli’nv, George … una’e squu ganela, dina,danvtli
segments.translation: There’s just three of these guys [Leroy and siblings] left. Brenda and then his brother George. That’s where he moved to, too.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, is that where he lives, too?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: George ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏣᏥᏍᏚᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ I come and got him. He was drinking ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮕ drugs, he was really bad. Ꮎ’Ꮫ “rent-a-home” building ᏥᏩᎩᏩᏒ and I fixed it ᎤᎾ ᏫᏥᏴᏍᏔᏅ and ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏦᏍᏓᏟᎲ trying to dry him up. Now he hasn’t—he’s been dry for 6 years.
segments.transliteration: George hena, ahani, hena, tsatsisdunv nigohilv tsatsisduhvsgv na I come and got him. He was drinking nowule’nv drugs, he was really bad. na’dv “rent-a-home” building tsiwagiwasv and I fixed it una witsiyvstanv and nigohilv’dv yusdi tsosdatlihv trying to dry him up. Now he hasn’t—he’s been dry for 6 years.
segments.translation: George, he was in jail, they were always putting him jail. I come and got him. He was drinking and doing drugs, he was really bad. That “rent-a-home” they call it. I bought a building and I fixed it up and I put him there. We were fighting all the time. Trying to dry him up. Now he’s been dry for six years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well praise the Lord!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is he the oldest?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Huh-uh. He’s the youngest.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: This one [Leroy] is the eldest of the three that are living.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: How old is he [George?]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: He said he’s 61.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Somewhere around there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏛᎾ,Ꮧ, … Ꮭ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏥᎪᎥ ᎦᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, Ꮭ ᏱᏥᏯᏅᏓᏗ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ,
segments.transliteration: etsulaha yusdi, tsogina,dvna,di, … tla elisdi, yigi, yitsigov gago gehv sgina, tla yitsiyanvdadi tsanv,ta,
segments.translation: We’re about the same age. Maybe if I saw him I’d know him, but I don’t remember him. Y’know?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: He was always in jail.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: He was always drunk.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did he go to school at Stilwell?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Chicago ᏥᏬᏥᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏧᏕᏅ ᏍᏊ Chicago ᎾᏅ, Brenda ᎤᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ she was born in Chicago, too.
segments.transliteration: vv Chicago tsiwotsinelv una tsudenv squu Chicago nanv, Brenda una squu tsosdadalv she was born in Chicago, too.
segments.translation: When we lived in Chicago, that’s where he was born. And my sister Brenda, too, she was born there.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Brenda ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ, Cherokee Nation ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ,
segments.transliteration: Brenda hena, ahani, Cherokee Nation tsulvwisdanehi,
segments.translation: Brenda, she works for Cherokee Nation.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It’s been a while since I’ve seen her. It’s been a few days ago, when she came in.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Retire-Ꮫ ᎨᎵ ᏛᏛᏁᎵ, ᏂᎦᎵ,--ᏥᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏓᏂᎳ, ᏃᏭ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Retire-dv geli dvdvneli, nigali,--tsiquisdi, hena, udanila, nowu, dohv?
segments.translation: I think she’s going to retire. She’s real sick now, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏦᎢ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᎤᎾ ᏂᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: vv tali,sgohi, tsoi nadetiyi una nidulvwi,sdaneho
segments.translation: She’s been working there for 23 years. 23 years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ, Jay Clinic ᎤᎾ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏱᎪᎯᏗ, ᏃᏭᏅ, retired ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ Cherokee Nation Clinic-Ꭲ.
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, digegv ditlv, Jay Clinic una dagilvwi,sdanelv tsosgohi, tsudetiyvda, yigohidi, nowunv, retired tsinawadvnelv Cherokee Nation Clinic-i.
segments.translation: Where I’m from, I worked at the Jay Clinic. After 30 years, I retired from Cherokee Nation Clinic.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was a doctor! [laughs]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Where they change out the inside… What do you call it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: What?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Where Brenda goes.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Oh…dialysis.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ,--ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, 3 years ᏁᏙᎰ ᏦᎢ, ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏁᏙᎰ ᎤᎾ ᏦᎢ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏒᎾ,ᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ, … Ꭴ--ᎤᏬᏰᏂ, ᏣᎩᎪᏛᏔᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮎ--Ꮎ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ this…this—this…
segments.transliteration: vv una hena,--una hena, 3 years nedoho tsoi, nadetiyi nedoho una tsoi, yuwaga,da, svna,dodawasdi, … u--uwoyeni, tsagigodvtanv ahani, na--na nadvnehv this…this—this…
segments.translation: Yeah, she’s been going to that for three years. Three times a week. She showed me her “hook up”/[arteriovenous fistula (AV)].

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They do put something in there.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: My daddy ᏍᏊ ᏥᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, … Little Rock ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ᏥᏭᎵᏍᏚᏡᏅ(50:31) ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᏥ--ᏧᏄᏢᏅ ᎧᏃᎨᏂ, and ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏓᏂ--they hook’em up. Three—three times a week: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. And … ᏍᎩᏃ … ᏥᏚᏔᏰᏎ’Ꮽ eight--ᏣᏁᎳ’Ꮫ ᏄᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ 8 years ᏥᏚᏔᏰᏎ’Ꮽ … ᎾᎯᏳ Amarillo, TX ᏥᏫ,ᏥᏁᎸ ᏥᏛᎩ,ᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ Ꮎ “ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏗᏥᎷᏨ ᎠᎭᏂ” ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏓᏍᏓᏰᏍᎬ … ᏧᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ one week ᏧᏲᎱᏒ
segments.transliteration: My daddy squu tsinadvnehv godawasga, … Little Rock ganaga,ti, tsiwulisdutlunv gohu,sdi, tsatsi--tsunutlvnv kanogeni, and unana tsidani--they hook’em up. Three—three times a week: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. And … sgino … tsidutayese’wu eight--tsanela’dv nudetiyvda, tsinudvnelv 8 years tsidutayese’wu … nahiyu Amarillo, TX tsiwi,tsinelv tsidvgi,danelv ditlanohedi na “nigada, diniyotli, ditsilutsv ahani” awanv,dv na dasdayesgv … tsusuli,gotsv one week tsuyohusv
segments.translation: My daddy, he did the same thing, Godawasg(a). He went to Little Rock and they put that thing (AV) in his arm, to hook him up. Three times a week: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. He just got tired of it. He did it for eight years. He just got tired of it. At that time, I was living in Amarillo, Texas. He called me, and said, “I want all of you children to come,” I knew he was tired. He quit, after one week, he passed away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ, ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ ᏓᎾᏍᏓᏰᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏗᎩᏗ, ᏃᏭ, ᏍᏗᎩᏗ, ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏪᏐᎸᏍᏓ, ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎢᎤᏁᏅᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ … ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎫ--ᎨᎫᏓᎸᏍᎬ dialysis ᏃᏭᎴ ᏓᎾᏍᏓᏰᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv ayv, hena, squu gatsiyoligv, tsigehv sgina, nanadvnehv, iga’dv danasdayesgv nowu nowule sdigidi, nowu, sdigidi, yana,dawesolvsda, iyusdi, nowule iunenvsdi,’e gehv … sgiyusdi, gegu--gegudalvsgv dialysis nowule danasdayesgv yusdi, nowule
segments.translation: I used to know a lot of folks who were doing that. They were all tired, they would rest a day and then they had to go back again. They were getting hooked up to dialysis. Then they were tired again.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁ Ꮎ Brenda ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: sgidv nuli,sdane na Brenda gohi tsigi,
segments.translation: The same things is happening to Brenda, today.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏓᏥᏁᎵᏒ ᎤᏓᎵᏍ’Ꭷ Ꮎ “kidney?” ᏓᏥᏁᎵᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ … ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ “Ꮭ” ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏂᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗᏍᎬ, Ꮎ I’m too old.
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, datsinelisv udalis’ka na “kidney?” datsinelisv sgina … ganaga,ti “tla” tsuna,dvnv nidigali,sdodisgv, na I’m too old.
segments.translation: I was going to give her one of my kidneys. Is Udali how you say Kidney? Yeah, I was going to give her one of my kidneys. The doctors said “no.” Because I’m too old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I guess that really is tiresome to do that.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Daddy was always tired.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They were always tired, yeah.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏦᎢ, ᎮᎾ, ᎾᏕᏘᏯ, ᎾᏛᏁᎲ, Brenda ᏦᎢ’ᏛᏢ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: tsoi, hena, nadetiya, nadvnehv, Brenda tsoi’dvtlv nadetiyi nowu
segments.translation: Brenda has been doing it for three years now. Yeah, it’s been about three years now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎤᏍᎦᏎ,Ꮧ’Ꮫ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏙᎲ? ᏃᏓᎦ,ᏎᏍᏛᎾ, ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv usgase,di’dv kali,setsi, dohv? nodaga,sesdvna, yigi,
segments.translation: Diabetes is real bad if you don’t take care of yourself.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is that what’s wrong with her, diabetes? Is she a diabetic?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: She has diabetes, right? Brenda.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I think so.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏴᏗ ᏣᏬᎮᎲ Brenda ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏴᎦᎯᎩ,
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv nusdv yvdi tsawohehv Brenda sgi nusdv hesdi, hena, yusdiwu gehv yvgahigi,
segments.translation: That’s what she told me, she said she couldn’t just eat anything.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She has to pick things she can eat.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: “I get mad sometimes. I hungry, I can’t eat what I want to eat,” ᏣᏬᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: “I get mad sometimes. I hungry, I can’t eat what I want to eat,” tsawohehv
segments.translation: “I get mad sometimes. I’m hungry, I can’t eat what I want to eat,” she told me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᏍᏊ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᎢᎦ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, “ᎨᎵ ᏱᏫᏥᎩ” ᏃᏭᎴ ᏁᎳᎩᏭ ᎨᎵᎰ
segments.transliteration: ayv, squu nawali,sdaneho iga gohu,sdi, awaduli tsanv,ta, “geli yiwitsigi” nowule nelagiwu geliho
segments.translation: That’s the same thing with me, I really want something [to eat,] y’know, but I don’t. I think, “I will go ahead and eat it,” but then I usually change my mind.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꭱ ᎾᎩᏪᏎᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, “ᏍᏗᎩᏗ’Ꮫ ᎥᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᏗᎢᏭ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’e nagiweselv na aganaga,ti, “sdigidi’dv vsgiyusdi,” udvnv “asenv, sdiiwu” tsadihv
segments.translation: That’s what the doctor told me, “Just eat a little bit. Just a little.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They tell you, “You can eat anything, but just this [gestures] much.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏴᎦᎪᏝ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏴ ᎨᏒ … ᏓᏤᏞ ᎾᎩᎬᎾ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᏭ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: tla yvgagotla sgi iga ayv gesv … datsetle nagigvna yigi, sgi yusdi, gohu,sdi sdiwu agisdi yigi,
segments.translation: You can’t get full eating a little bit. Might as well not eat it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “It’s just like an appetizer,” is what I tell them. [laughs]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎤᎾ Stillwater Indian Tacos sale ᏥᏄᏅᏅ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᎵᏊ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏛᏁ,Ꮧ Ꮎ Anita Christie and benefit ᏥᏄᏅᏅ let’s see ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎨᎵ ᏥᏓᎩᏩᏒ indian tacos, and they brought them to the house. And I called, ᎾᎥ ᏗᏂᏁᎳ, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᏂᎬ ᏱᎩ, indian tacos ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎢᎦᏓ, Boy, ᎪᎢᎭ ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏄᏮ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏒ
segments.transliteration: na una Stillwater Indian Tacos sale tsinunvnv anitsalagi’nv, tsigehv daliquu tsunilosv gohu,sdi, hena, dina,dadvne,di na Anita Christie and benefit tsinunvnv let’s see sgohi, geli tsidagiwasv indian tacos, and they brought them to the house. And I called, nav dininela, hesdi, hena, ilvhiyu unigv yigi, indian tacos aniyonega, igada, Boy, goiha tsini,dunuwv (uyetsi,sgv) tsunanigisv
segments.translation: They had an Indian taco sale in Stillwater. They were Cherokees from Tahlequah, they were kin to Anita Christie. They were doing it for a benefit. I bought 10 Indian tacos. I called my neighbors, some of them were white people, they had never eaten Indian tacos. Boy, they had grease all over their clothes. [laughs] Then they left.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Do you all like Wild Onion?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I really like it.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: They’re already eating it, aren’t they?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, already.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It’s been awhile already, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏅᏃᎯ, ᎾᎥ’Ꮲ park ᏱᏅᎦ, and go get it.
segments.transliteration: eliwu ‘lvtlv nvnohi, nav’tlv park yinvga, and go get it.
segments.translation: Where there is room by the road somewhere to find Wild Onion, park, to go get it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Football player, this one.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, give me a screwdriver or something.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, give me a screwdriver or something.
segments.translation: Yeah, give me a screwdriver or something.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏔᎵᎭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ,--ᏦᎢᎭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ, ᎠᎩᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ … ᎩᎶ ᏣᎩᏁᎸ--ᏦᎩᏂᏁᎸ’Ꮥ … ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎤᏅᎦᎸ:Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎦ--ᏌᏭ’Ꮓ ᎦᏳᎳ, ᎤᎬᎭᎸᎲ ᎨᎲ ᎾᏅ ᏐᎢ, ᎩᎶ ᏦᎩᏂᏁᎸ ᎤᏓᏅᎦᎸᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎠᎦᎷᏱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, taliha yuwaga,da,--tsoiha yuwagada, agigv sgina … gilo tsaginelv--tsogininelv’de … nigada, unvgalv:di, tsigehv iga--sawu’no gayula, ugvhalvhv gehv nanv soi, gilo tsogininelv udanvgalvda, squu gehv asenv uwasa, agaluyi,sdi, gehv
segments.translation: Yeah, I’ve eaten it two or three times now. Someone gave it to me, or they gave it to us. All of it was clean. One [bag] was already cut. And then we got another one, we had to cut that up.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They say they’re selling them for $30.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᎨ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎪᏪᎵ, ᏧᏂᏅ,Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏓᎵᏆ, ᎦᏚᎲ ᏴᎦᎷᎪ ᎪᏪᎵ, ᏧᏔᎾ, ᏧᏂ--ᏚᏂᏯᎸ *ᎯᎢᏭ* ᏱᎩᏗ, ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ
segments.transliteration: age’dv na goweli, tsuninv,dv na daliqua, gaduhv yvgalugo goweli, tsutana, tsuni--duniyalv *hiiwu* yigidi, sgohi, adela
segments.translation: There was a post/notice in Tahlequah right when you get into town. The post said they were selling this [gestures] size for $10.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Gah lee, man! ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ, ᏦᎢ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᎨᎵ ᏣᏩ--ᏣᏩᏈᏴᎲ *ᏍᎩ* ᏱᎩᏗ,
segments.transliteration: Gah lee, man! ayv’nv, tsoi, adela geli tsawa--tsawaquiyvhv *sgi* yigidi,
segments.translation: Gah-lee, man! I paid $3 dollars and it was this [gestures] much.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮫ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏗᎦᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏯᏩᏕᏔᏌ, ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏗᎩᎬᏩᎶ,ᏙᏗ ᏱᎨᎵ ᎠᏴ,
segments.transliteration: awanv,dv sdayi digalvwi,sdane,di dohv? asenv, yawadetasa, sgi iga digigvwalo,dodi yigeli ayv,
segments.translation: I know it’s hard work, but I wouldn’t feel right selling it for that much.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ Ꮎ ᎪᏓᏩᏍᎦ, ᎧᎵ,ᏍᏓᏯ’Ꮕ … ᎤᏓᏈᏍᏗ,’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ … Lyon Switch Ꮎ railroad ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎾᎥ
segments.transliteration: na’e agi,sdi tsigehv tsitsisdelihv na godawasga, kali,sdaya’nv … udaquisdi,’dv tsigehv … Lyon Switch na railroad tsulohisdi nav
segments.translation: When I was little, I used to help Godawasg(a) and Kal(i)sday(a). It was annoying to get it in Lyon Switch, by the railroad tracks.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏱᏍᏓᏛᏁᎴ ᏂᎯ ᎠᏓ, ᏗᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎦᏂ,ᏗᏅᏗ, ᎡᏘ’Ᏼ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᏗᏂᎬᏩᎵ,Ꮫ ᎦᏒᏓ,
segments.transliteration: nowule’nv, squu … tla yawanv,ta, sgina, yisdadvnele nihi ada, disquali,sdi, digani,dinvdi, eti’yv tsigehv hisgi, adela dinigvwali,dv gasvda,
segments.translation: And also, I don’t know if you all have done it, but splitting wood to sell. A long time ago, they sold a rick for $5.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: That’s hard work.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Now, they sell about $100.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah,

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Some…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Two years ago, ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂ--ᎠᏂ--ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ, I hired them. OKC. $135 ᏥᏥᏂ,ᏕᎬ a rick [of wood.] It’s hard work.
segments.transliteration: Two years ago, tali, ani--ani--anisgaya, I hired them. OKC. $135 tsitsini,degv a rick [of wood.] It’s hard work.
segments.translation: Two years ago, I hired two men in OKC. I was selling ricks of wood for $135. It’s hard work.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah. ᏙᏳ’ᏛᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏏᏛ Ꮟ ᎡᎳᏗ, ᏄᏅᏁ,Ꮧ ᏧᎾ,ᏚᎵᎲ ᎤᎾᏈᏗ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮦ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏗᎦᎸ--ᏗᎦᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ, ᎠᏓ, ᏥᏙᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᎬ ᎤᎦᎴᏴᏍᏙᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ‘ᏡᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᏓᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᏗ, ᏧᏩᏅ,ᎦᏢ ᏃᏭ … ᏃᏭᎴ *ᎯᎢ* ᏱᎩᏗ, ᏃᏭ, ᏓᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏗᎬᎷᏱ,ᏍᏓᎯᏓᏍᏗ, ‘Ꮧ ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮦ ᎢᎦ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏗᎦᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. doyu’dvhv nahiyu tsigehv hesdi, sidv si eladi, nunvne,di tsuna,dulihv unaquidi hesdi, hena, yunanv,te ilvhiyu tsadi iga digalv--digalvwi,sdane,di, ada, tsidosquali,sgv ugaleyvsdodi, hena, ‘tlugv nowule udasquali,sdi, tsuwanv,gatlv nowu … nowule *hii* yigidi, nowu, dasquali,sdi, nowule digvluyi,sdahidasdi, ‘di yunanv,te iga sdayi digalvwi,sdane,di nahiyu
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. Back then, somebody wanted to pay less. They didn’t know how hard it was to cut wood. You had to cut down the tree, and then cut off all the limbs, then you cut measured pieces, then you had to use the axe. They didn’t know. It was a lot of work back then.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏗᎨᏛᏍᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏦᏦᏢᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏙᎦᏛᏐᏅ
segments.transliteration: digedvsgi, hena, tsotsotlvsgv, tsigehv sgi dogadvsonv
segments.translation: We made fence posts. We grew up doing that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᎡᏘ’Ᏼ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ, ᏗᎨᏛᏍᎩ, ᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ … ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮕ Ꮎ ᏗᎦ--ᏣᏗᎲ ᎨᎵ ᏂᎯ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ, … ᏗᎦᏣᏄᎵ, ᏗᎬ,Ꮧ, ᏗᏗᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ,
segments.transliteration: sgi hena, nanadvnehv, tsigehv tsuna,tana, eti’yv tsigehv digegv ditlv, digedvsgi, danotlvsgv … nowule’nv na diga--tsadihv geli nihi gohu,sdi, yusdi, … digatsanuli, digv,di, didisdi doyu’dv tsidanotlvsgv,
segments.translation: That’s what the older ones did, they made these fence posts. And also, I think you said it earlier, they made those things with the railroad. Ties.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᏗᏗᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ railroad tracks ᏗᏗᏍᏗ,’Ꮫ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎦᎷᏱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎦᏅᎯᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎷᏱ,ᏍᏗ, … *ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ* ᏱᎾᏛᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎢᏣᎦ,ᏙᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᎠᎭᏂ!” ᏯᏓ, ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎢᏣᎦ,ᏙᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᎯᎢ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎮᏍᏗ, ᎠᏴ,--ᎠᏴ, ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲᎾ, ᎨᎮᏍᏗ,” ᏗᎪᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ railroad ties. Truck-Ꭲ ᏥᏓᎯᎵᏙᎲ ᏥᎦᏂ,ᏗᏅ(57:50)
segments.transliteration: Yeah, didisdi’dv eliwu tsanoheho sginana railroad tracks didisdi,’dv edoda, tsigehv tsigotlvsgv, tsigehv nudale hena, yusdi, galuyi,sdi, sginana ganvhida, hena, galuyi,sdi, … *hii’dv* yinadvga, tsigehv “itsaga,dosdesdi, ahani!” yada, edoda, tsigehv “itsaga,dosdesdi, hii hena, nitsadvnehesdi, ayv,--ayv, yawadulihvna, gehesdi,” digotlvsgv na railroad ties. Truck-i tsidahilidohv tsigani,dinv
segments.translation: Yeah, ties. My dad used to make those, railroad ties. And the axe for that was different. It was kinda long. He would do this [gestures] to it. “Y’all watch what I’m doing,” he say, our dad. “When I don’t want to do this, y’all will be doing it,” he said. Every three weeks, he would bring food.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s what they were doing.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,Ꮚ ᏳᎾ,ᏓᎨᏓ, ᏄᎾ, ᏱᏓᏲᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎢ’Ꮕ ᎠᏔᎷᎩᏍᎩ, ᎦᏢ,
segments.transliteration: sgohitsi,quu yuna,dageda, nuna, yidayoga, tsigehv goi’nv atalugisgi, gatlv,
segments.translation: 100lbs of…potatoes and grease, that was in a tin bucket.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was a tall bucket.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Bag of flour and…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: …beans.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Beans.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏚᏯ Boy, ᎠᏎ ᏚᏯ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏗᎩᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ … ᏃᏭᎴᏅ … ᎢᏌ, ᏗᎦᏅ,ᏔᏅ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᏓᎨᏓ, ᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏧᏬᏚᎯ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏕᎦᏇᏅ,Ꮫ ᎢᏌ, ᎾᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᎵ,ᏌᏅ ᏌᏭ’Ꮓ ᎠᎿᏬ ᏥᏩᎪᏢᏍᎬ, ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭼ,ᏔᏅ yeah.
segments.transliteration: duya Boy, ase duya osda digisdi, tsigehv nahiyu … nowulenv … isa, diganv,tanv talisgohi, yudageda, geli tsigehv sgigadu’le yigi, tsuwoduhi, tsigehv tsidegaquenv,dv isa, nanv etsi tsigehv yuli,sanv sawu’no ahnawo tsiwagotlvsgv, squu sgina gv,tanv yeah.
segments.translation: Beans. Boy, beans were good to eat back then. And a bag of flour, it was 20lb or 15lb. Anyway, the bags were real pretty. Mom, after she used it up, she would make clothes out of it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏥᎦᏗ ᎡᎵᏏ, “ᏩᏑᏯᎩ” ᏯᏬᏌ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏌᏃ ᏯᏬᏢᎾᏌ, ᏍᎩᎾᏃ ᎤᏩᏌ,
segments.transliteration: sginana tsigadi elisi, “wasuyagi” yawosa, tsigehv asano yawotlvnasa, sginano uwasa,
segments.translation: My grandma used to tell me, “Pick one.” Then she’d make me a dress out of it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎰᏩ ‘Ꮲ ᏱᏭᎾ,ᏕᎨ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏃᏢᏍᎬ,
segments.transliteration: sgidv tla hena, doyu, nahiyu tsanehv hesdi, hena, gohu,sdi, howa ‘tlv yiwuna,dege gohu,sdi, hena, tsanotlvsgv,
segments.translation: Right. Yeah, people back then, they didn’t throw things away. They made things out of it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎢᏌ, ᏥᏚᏂᏢ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎦᏘ, Ꮭ ᏯᏅ,ᏓᏗ? ᎢᏌ, ᎧᎵ ᏧᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ, trash can ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎢᏤ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎧᎵ’Ꮫ ᏳᏝ, ᎤᎾ ᏦᏥᎴᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: nadv squu isa, tsidunitlv hii yigati, tla yanv,dadi? isa, kali tsutlv tsigehv elisi, trash can iyusdi, asenv, itse tsigehv tsanv,ta, kali’dv yutla, una tsotsilesgv
segments.translation: And they used to have the flour in a big bucket/jug. You don’t remember it? My grandmother used to have it full of flour. It looked like a trashcan. But it was new, y’know, it was full of flour and we’d get it out of there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮎ Walmart ᎠᎨᎢ ᏗᎿᏬ ᏗᎩᏩᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: na gohi tsigi, na Walmart agei dihnawo digiwasgo
segments.translation: Nowadays, we go to Walmart and buy clothes.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏣᏓᎾᎾ’Ꮫ ᎾᎥ ᎢᎾ ᏕᎦᏛᏒ ᎾᎥ ‘ᏙᎩ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ? ᎠᏭ Woodpecker-Ꭲ?(59:23)
segments.transliteration: tsadanana’dv nav ina degadvsv nav ‘dogi dudov sgina? awu Woodpecker-i?
segments.translation: They had a store, near where we grew up. What was it called? By Woodpecker?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Albany?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏣᏓᎾᎾ ᎢᎾ, ᏦᎦᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᎢᎦ--ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏏᏅᏓ,Ꮂ ᏱᎪᎯᏗ, ᏦᏥᏓᏁᎳᏗᎲ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏲᏣᏓᏅᎾ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᎾᎾ ᎡᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: sawu tsadanana ina, tsogadvsidolv iga--nigohilv hena, yusdi, sinvda,hv yigohidi, tsotsidaneladihv ‘lvtlv nowule yotsadanvna, nahiyu tsigehv adanana ehe tsigehv una
segments.translation: Yeah. There was a store there where we grew up around. We would just live there a month and then move again. There was a store there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where was it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Lyon Switch.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Lyon Switch.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Do you know where Buck Scraper lived?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏫᎦᎶᏒ down the hill across the railroad tracks. It’s on the right-hand side. It’s been a long a time, ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: wigalosv down the hill across the railroad tracks. It’s on the right-hand side. It’s been a long a time, dohv?
segments.translation: Past that, down the hill and across the railroad tracks. It’s on the right-hand side. It’s been a long time, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ᏺ Bunch-ᎢᎮ ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍ ᏍᎩᎾ? Choate’s ᏥᏄᏅᏅ Felix Choate
segments.transliteration: na’yo Bunch-ihe hanv,dadis sgina? Choate’s tsinunvnv Felix Choate
segments.translation: Do you remember Bunch Store the Choate’s had? Felix Choate.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I don’t remember the one in Lyon Switch.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎢᎾ’Ꮫ ᏣᏓᎾᎾ ᎤᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ … ᎠᏓᎾᎾ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ina’dv tsadanana una squu tsiganelv … adanana tsiganelv dohv?
segments.translation: Yeah, the store owner lived there in the store. He lived in the store, right?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏑᏓᎵ ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏑᎵᎶᏓ, gas.
segments.transliteration: sudali iyadanv,di tsigehv na suliloda, gas.
segments.translation: A gallon of gas was six cents.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᏍᏊ ᏴᏟᎦ, ᎧᎵ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: tali, adela squu yvtliga, kali tsini,gali,sdihv dohv?
segments.translation: You could fill up your tank on just $2.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Man.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We would drive around all week with that.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏂᎬ’Ꮫ ᏯᏟᏓ, ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ, truck ᎠᎩᎭ, ᏐᏁᎳ, let’s see…it’s 9 miles a gallon.
segments.transliteration: nigv’dv yatlida, ayv’nv, truck agiha, sonela, let’s see…it’s 9 miles a gallon.
segments.translation: You could run around all over. The truck I have, let’s see…it’s nine miles a gallon.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Man! ᎠᏴ, ᎠᏩᏦᏙ pickup 20 miles an hour – 20 miles a gallon.
segments.transliteration: Man! ayv, awatsodo pickup 20 miles an hour – 20 miles a gallon.
segments.translation: Man! My truck, it’s 20 miles an hour – 20 miles a gallon.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: That’s not bad.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s good!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ -- ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏭ ᎠᎢᏒ ᏴᏕᎳᎰ’Ꮫ … ᏳᏓᎭ 19 ᏱᎨᏐ
segments.transliteration: ase’dv -- asenv awu aisv yvdelaho’dv … yudaha 19 yigeso
segments.translation: You can tell going down the road. Then sometimes, it’s 19 miles a gallon.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s alright, ain’t it? Seems like it.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: What kind is it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I have a Ford Lariat F-150.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Me too, I have a Ford.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘ᏙᏗ ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ Ꮎ motor … ᎤᏟᏂᎩᏓ, ᏳᏟᏓᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎡᏯᏄᎳ, ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏧᏟᏓᏍᏗ, ᎦᏢ motor. Co-something.
segments.transliteration: ‘dodi tsidanoseho na motor … utlinigida, yutlidasdi yusdi, eyanula, iyusdi, tsutlidasdi, gatlv motor. Co-something.
segments.translation: It’s got, what do they call it? It’s got a heavy-duty motor. Co-something.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: I know it, ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮤ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏚᏙᎠ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, (…)[1:01:31] ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᏔᎾ truck ᎠᎩᎭ Four-wheel drive, 2 quarter-ton. ᎾᏅ trailer ᏓᎩᎭ, ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏕᏥᏂ,ᏏᏂᏙᎲ … ᏩᎧ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏕᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏞᎦ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏗᏩᎳᏏ,ᏕᎾ, they got bad. Knee replacement, ᏥᏂ,ᏓᏮᏁᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ, then my shoulder. I was pressed in. ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏥᏂ,ᏓᎩᏂ,ᏗᏅᏒ ᏩᎧ,
segments.transliteration: I know it, awanv,ta yusdi dudoa na sgihena, yusdi, (…) asenv, utana truck agiha Four-wheel drive, 2 quarter-ton. nanv trailer dagiha, nigohi,lv detsini,sinidohv … waka, hena, tsidetsinatlav tlega, asenv, diwalasi,dena, they got bad. Knee replacement, tsini,dawvnelv ahani, then my shoulder. I was pressed in. nigada, tsini,dagini,dinvsv waka,
segments.translation: I know what you’re talking about. I have a big truck. Four-wheel drive, two quarter-ton. And I also have trailers, I pull them around all the time. I had cows for a while, but then my feet got really bad. I had a knee replacement and then my shoulder, I was pressed in. I sold them all [the cows.]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: … ᎯᎾ’Ꮓ ᎣᏂ ᏓᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᏂ, … ᏴᏓ, ᏓᏓᏛᏛᎲᏍᎦ,(1:02:09) ᏔᎵ, ᏍᎪᎯᏴ ᏭᎾᏕᏘᏴᎲ ᎠᎢᏎᏍᏗᏭᏍᎪ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ? ᏫᏛᏍᎪᎸᏥ’Ꭸ ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏗᏬᏂᎯ,?
segments.transliteration: … hina’no oni dasdvyadvdvni, … yvda, dadadvdvhvsga, tali, sgohiyv wunadetiyvhv aisesdiwusgo, tsalagi, gawonihisdi, sdelisgo? widvsgolvtsi’ge sdelisgo atsalagi, tsidiwonihi,?
segments.translation: This is the last thing I’m going to ask you all: We say, we ask… in 20 years, do you all think they will still be speaking Cherokee? Or will our language disappear?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I don’t think it will ever disappear. [laughs] Is what I think.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’ᏛᏴ if I can helpt it? No. I want it to continue. ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎠᏃᎵ,Ꭼ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏬᏂᎲ … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏳᏓᎭ ᏱᏩᏮᎨᏩ,ᏍᎪ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏬᏂᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dvyv if I can helpt it? No. I want it to continue. nigohilv tsiwonisgo nanv anitsutsa, anoli,gv nigohilv tsiwonihv … asenv, yudaha yiwawvgewa,sgo asenv, nigohilv tsiwonihv tsalagi, ganeli,dihv
segments.translation: Me, if I can help it? No. I want it to continue. I speak all the time. Those boys, they understand. I forget things all the time, but I try to speak Cherokee all the time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about you?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Me, I will never forget. I grew up speaking it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎢ’Ꮓ ᎣᏂ, ᏣᎾᎢ, … ᎢᎸᎯᏳ’Ꭸ ᏫᏛᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᎢ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ? ᏃᏭ, ‘ᏢᏴ’Ꮓ ᏙᎯ, ᏂᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᏗᏬᏂᎲ?
segments.transliteration: hii’no oni, tsanai, … ilvhiyu’ge widvna,deloquai, tsalagi, uniwonihisdi sdelisgo? nowu, ‘tlvyv’no dohi, nidagali,stani, tsalagi, idiwonihv?
segments.translation: These one’s coming up, do you all think they will learn to speak Cherokee? Or is it going to disappear someday?

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I would say, no.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: I hope not.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, I hope not.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Like you said, the boys really understand…

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, they really do.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But they should speak it, too.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏓᏁᎶᎲᏍᎦ, ᏣᎳᎩ,’Ꭱ ᏯᏪᏡᎦ, ᏂᎦᏓ, they’ll be looking at me.
segments.transliteration: squatlesdi, hena, yidanelohvsga, tsalagi,’e yawetluga, nigada, they’ll be looking at me.
segments.translation: When they play ball, I’m yelling in Cherokee. Everybody will be looking at me.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏴ, ᏍᏊ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏣᏩᎳᏍᎦᎸᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ,’Ꮫ ᏦᏥᏬᏂᎲ ᎦᏌᏛ(1:03:44) ᏙᎩᎧᏅ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, ᎠᏂᏳᏁᎦ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ayv, squu sawu yuwaga,da, tsawalasgalvhv tsalagi,’dv tsotsiwonihv gasadv dogikanv anisoi, aniyunega,
segments.translation: Yeah, one time we were all talking Cherokee, playing ball. The whites were all looking at us.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏓᎩᎧᎭ, they’re black belts in Tae Kwon Do, ᏂᎬ ᏦᎨᏙᎸ U.S. – tournements. Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏂᎾ medals
segments.transliteration: nanv anitsutsa, dagikaha, they’re black belts in Tae Kwon Do, nigv tsogedolv U.S. – tournements. tsi,quisdi, hena, dunina medals
segments.translation: The two boys I have, they’re black belts in Tae Kwon Do. We’ve been all over the U.S. at different tournaments. They both have a lot of medals.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be!

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎠᎬᏱ the first time ᎤᏅᏌ, ᏧᎾᏟᏢ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ ᏧᎾᎵ,ᎪᏔᏅ(1:04:17) ᏗᏍᏚᏗ ᎠᎾᏟᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏥᏩᎩᎷᏨ, … ᏥᏩᏩᎴᏫᏍᏙᏔᏅ ᎠᎾᏟᎲ
segments.transliteration: asenv, agvyi the first time unvsa, tsunatlitlv gali,tsode nigada,’dv tsunali,gotanv disdudi anatlihv sginana ayetli tsiwagilutsv, … tsiwawalewisdotanv anatlihv
segments.translation: But the first time, they fought each other at the house. They tore up all the doors, so I got in the middle and I made them quit fighting.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They really meant it?

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah! ᏍᏚᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ ᏥᏚᏂᎶᎾ,ᏔᏅ walls-Ꭲ ᏧᏂᎿᎸᏒ’Ꭱ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎴ “’ᏙᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏔᏛᏁᎵ?” – “You’re going to get out. If you don’t get out, I got a shotgun in there,” I told them. – But, they haven’t done it anymore. ᎤᎾᎵ I mean, ᎡᏧᎳ, ᎮᎾ, they make good money. ᎠᏎᏅ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah! sdudi nigada,’dv tsidunilona,tanv walls-i tsunihnalvsv’e agvyi sgi nuna,dvnele “’donv yusdi, tadvneli?” – “You’re going to get out. If you don’t get out, I got a shotgun in there,” I told them. – But, they haven’t done it anymore. unali I mean, etsula, hena, they make good money. asenv,
segments.translation: Yeah! They tore up all the doors and walls, too. They were really mad at each other, when they first did it. They asked, “What are you going to do?” – “You’re going to get out. If you don’t get out, I got a shotgun in there,” I told them. – But, they haven’t done it anymore. They are good friends and both of them make good money.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: They’re both grown up.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏎᏅ, they’re still at the house. They take care of Mom and Dad.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, asenv, they’re still at the house. They take care of Mom and Dad.
segments.translation: Yeah, they still live at the house. They both take care of Mom and Dad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s good.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: They do take care of us.
segments.transliteration: They do take care of us.
segments.translation: They do take care of us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎣᎩᏂ,ᏓᎵᏏ, ‘Ꮲ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏃᏭ, Little Debbie’s ᏥᏕᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, Gentry. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᏂᏍᏕᎸᎯᏙᎰ ᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎣᏏ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ayv, hena, squu ogini,dalisi, ‘tlv tali,sgohi, sawu yudetiyvda, nowu, Little Debbie’s tsidelvwi,sdanehi, Gentry. sgina oginisdelvhidoho sdi yusdi, osi sgi hena, yinana,dvne
segments.translation: Yeah, our grandchild, he’s 21 years old and working at Little Debbie’s in Gentry. He helps us out, some. It’s good when they do that.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏛ’Ᏺ I-I-I-We feel like we’ve done a good job. ᏓᎾ,ᏛᏍᎬ ᏥᏳ ᏧᏩᏒ Ꮎ $25,000 ᏧᏈᏴᎲ ᏥᏳ “Dad, we’re going to take you on a boat. - ᏥᏳ ᏓᏓᏣᏂ,” – “Good! ᏍᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᏗ, ᏓᏩᏑᎴᏍᏗ,” ᏥᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: osdv’yo I-I-I-We feel like we’ve done a good job. dana,dvsgv tsiyu tsuwasv na $25,000 tsuquiyvhv tsiyu “Dad, we’re going to take you on a boat. - tsiyu dadatsani,” – “Good! sdanv,tesdi, dawasulesdi,” tsigatsiyohelv
segments.translation: We feel like we’ve done a good job, raising them. He bought a boat, he paid $25,000. “Dad, we’re going to take you on a boat. - tsiyu dadatsan(i)” – “Good, I’m going to wear diapers.”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ‘ᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᎬᏮᎨᏩ’Ꭱ ᏣᎳᎩ,’Ᏺ … ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᏯᏩᎨᏩ’Ꭱ
segments.transliteration: sgidv ‘lvhiyu yigvwvgewa’e tsalagi,’yo … yonega, hena, yawagewa’e
segments.translation: I will never forget the Cherokee language. But I would forget English.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᏊ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: asenv, squu tsi,quisdi, hena, anitsalagi, yonega, aniwonihv squu gohi, tsigi,
segments.translation: There’s a lot of Cherokees that speak English, nowadays.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᎭᎴ ᎾᏮᎨᏩ,Ꮢ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗ, ᏱᎨᎮ … ᎯᏲᎵᎦ, Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ,? ᏗᏍᏓᏕᏠ,ᏆᎡ ᎡᎵᏭ -- Darrell Guffy
segments.transliteration: ayv,’dv hale nawvgewa,sv (uniyetsi,sgv) tla gilo tsalagi, tsilinohedi, yigehe … hiyoliga, na osdinela,? disdadetlo,quae eliwu -- Darrell Guffy
segments.translation: Me, I almost forgot it, [laughter] there’s nobody to talk to. Do you know my husband? You probably went to school together. Darrell Guffy.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Who was it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Darrell Guffy.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Oh, yes, ᎤᏙᏗᏍᎪ, Bill [Guffy] ᏥᏚᏙᎥ Yes.
segments.transliteration: Oh, yes, udodisgo, Bill [Guffy] tsidudov Yes.
segments.translation: Oh, yeah, his dad’s name was Bill Guffy? Yes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, I told him. He said, “Ooh!” - I went to school at Greasy.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Where?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Oh, you did.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “I always wanted to beat him,” I told him.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: How’s Darrell doing?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎣᏏᏭ, ᏔᎵ, ᏧᎸᏓᎸᏅ He had two strokes. ᎣᏏᏭ ᎨᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.transliteration: osiwu, tali, tsulvdalvnv He had two strokes. osiwu geho yudaha
segments.translation: He’s alright. He’s had two strokes. He’s alright, sometimes.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.text: Yeah, ᎾᏅ ᎤᏙᏓ, worked Coke ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nanv udoda, worked Coke tsigehv
segments.translation: His dad used to sell Coca-Cola.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was a principal.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Yeah, he was a principal.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏦᎢ’Ꮫ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Ꮎ retire ᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᏃᏭ,
segments.transliteration: vv tsoi’dv yuwaga,da, na retire nudvnelv nowu,
segments.translation: Darrell has retired three times now.

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Post Office-Ꭲ ᎮᎾ, 30 years, Post Master ᏧᏴᏢ ᏃᏭᎾᏅ retire ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᎨᎵ’Ꮫ ᏔᎵ, ᏱᏅᏓ, ᏃᏭᎴ Auditor ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ casinos, audit ᏥᏚᏮᏁᎸ -- ᏩᎩ’Ꮕ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏥᏃᏍᏗᏁᎩᎡᎲ 30 years -- ᎭᎴ ᎾᎩᏅᏍᏓᏕᎲ(1:07:25) (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: Post Office-i hena, 30 years, Post Master tsuyvtlv nowunanv retire tsinudvnelv geli’dv tali, yinvda, nowule Auditor tsigehv na casinos, audit tsiduwvnelv -- wagi’nv nowule tsinosdinegiehv 30 years -- hale naginvsdadehv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: He was at the post office for 30 years. He was the Postmaster. Then he retired, but then two months later he was the auditor at the casino. He audited them. Then we milked cows for 30 years. That almost killed me. [laughs]

segments.speaker: leroy-sanders
segments.translation: Tell him I said hello.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, I’ll tell him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well I appreciate it. I appreciate us all talking.

segments.speaker: felix-sanders
segments.translation: I appreciate you all, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ, ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏍᏛᏯᏛᏗ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ,’Ꮫ ᏨᏌ, ᏥᏍᏗᏬᏂᎲ ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: galieliga, doyu hena, tla howa gohu,sdi, sdvyadvdi yini,gali,sda, galieliga,’dv tsvsa, tsisdiwonihv nowu
segments.translation: I’m glad I didn’t have to really ask you all anything. You all just talked on your own.
